# tofu parity

| side | exe | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| a | E:\tofu-scratchpad\c\parity\tofu-develop.exe | 028aed35d6e20af2b37394c07e4d8fc68e140535ef7a5a741dcc599d07bab258 |
| b | E:\tofu-scratchpad\c\parity\tofu-2112.exe | 79f864e502a6f0bb50b979f9f8c07639ec9825cc50605f323322e5c2691a8b3f |

Machine DESKTOP-AHUN9RO, windows/amd64. Each case runs once per build, a then b, one process at a time, in a home, an APPDATA and a project made fresh for it, with no key and every network URL pointed at a refused port. No call is discarded as a warm up. Masked: paths, versions, commit, Go version, dates, clock times, ago, milliseconds, KB sizes, pids, uuids, session ids and names, tool refs; a byte count may differ by 64; a transcript that holds a session name, whose length is random, is compared as words, so its line breaks may move; serve notifications are sorted, without seq and session, and the session.listed broadcast is dropped because how often it fires follows timing; files written are compared by path, without sqlite -shm and -wal files and shells/pruned, which follow timing too.

**943/1000 equal**, 57 diff, 0 error, 10 manual, 12 unreachable

The repository holds only those and the salt, so committing `<repo>/.tofu` needs no\n`.gitignore`; the summary tree the lead reads, its view and its lock live in the home. A\nrepository id carries a tag, `MEMORY1`, so two homes never write the same.\n\nWhere two entries disagree, the first of `user-local`, `project-local`, `project-global`,\n`user-global` wins. `library/memory/scopes@1.yaml` sets each scope's precedence, the view budget the\nlead reads and where an entry is promoted next. Every summary one pass needs goes out in one batched call, and a summary that drops a name its two lines held, such as a file or a function, is asked for again on its own. -     "markdown": "## What it is\n\nEvery request `tofu serve --stdio` answers; `tofu docs serve` says how to start it, `tofu serve --schema`\ncarries every field. Reads, reloads, the `session.*` and `memory.*` reads, `mention.resolve`, `shell.run`,\n`learn.scan`, `setup.check` and the logins answer out of order, so none holds `turn.stop`. Every request\nanswers a typed result with no envelope, and a verb that fails errs with its problems.\n\n## Where it lives\n\n- `initialize`: takes `client`, `versions` and `capabilities`, where `questions` says it answers `tofu/askPerson`; answers `protocol`, `tofu`, `project` and `capabilities`, one name a family of methods\n- `session.list`: takes `search`, `limit` and `kind`; answers `head` and `sessions`, each `id`, `name`,\n  `handle`, `task`, `turns`, `lastAt`, `wire`, `model`, `costUsd`, `outcome`, `open` (here), `running`,\n  `members` (every tofu, desk and serve joined to it) and `kind`, `main` or `side`; a side chat adds `parent`, `owns`, `preset`, and a fork names the generation it came from as `parent`. It stops reading once `limit` rows are found\n- side chats (capability `side`): `session.branch` takes `session`, `kind: \"side\"`, `seed` (`summary` or\n  `none`), `owns` or `preset`, `name`, `model`, `effort` and `at` `{item}`, the parent's event to branch from\n  (the `item` `mention.resolve` answers), whose summary stops there; answers `session`, `handle`, `parent`\n  `{session, event}`, `owns`, `preset`, `carried`, `model` and `effort`; `session.open` of the side chat\n  picks its `model`. `tofu session branch` takes `--model`, `--effort`, `--at`. `session.access` takes `session`\n  and `owns` or `preset`, `read` with neither, and errs while that chat's turn runs\n- `session.open`: takes `session` (none starts a fresh one), `asking` and `replay`, how many of the newest\n  lines it sends; answers `session`, `fresh` and `members`, each `{process, kind, joined}` with `kind` `tui`, `desk` or `serve`: the session runs in the project's `tofu host`, every client joins it as a member, replaying the session and then streaming its events live, and `turn.send`, `turn.stop` and answers run there. `session.member` tells every client the new `members` whenever one joins or leaves, and `session.state` carries them too. When the last member leaves, the host cancels the session's turn, naming that member, and ends its shells. While a\n  turn runs, the new one opens beside it (capability `sessions`) and one already open here takes the focus;\n  a request with no `session` means the one opened last. `session.close` takes `session` and `stop`, and\n  errs while that session's turn runs unless `stop` is true, and on the only session open\n- `session.state`, the answer to `resync`: `running` and its `turn`, `asking`, the `pick`, waiting approvals,\n  `standing` answers (`target`, `decision`, `given`, `until`, `kept`: `session`, beside the session, read back when it reopens, carried into\n  its compaction and never into another session, or `process`, held until tofu restarts), open `questions`, sub-agents, kept shells (each with `port` once tofu learns it and `ref`, the quote of the call that started it), the context and the cron jobs\n- `approval.list` (capability `standing`): answers `session` and `standing`, every answer standing there, as `session.state` does, and `/permissions` shows; `approval.revoke` takes `target` and answers the one it took back, or errs when none stands there\n- `session.set`: takes `asking`, `wire`, `model` and `effort`, held for later turns and cron fires; `session.settings` tells every client\n- `session.rename`: takes `session` and `name`, and names the whole family\n- `session.compact` (capability `compact`): takes `session` and `focus`, kept whole in every old tool result that names it; answers `kind`, `results`, `focus`, `focused`, `tokensBefore`, `tokensAfter`, `into`, and errs on a session opened beside the first. `session.fork` (capability `fork`): takes `session`; opens a new line carrying what `session.compact` carries, even with nothing to shrink, and answers the same with `kind: \"fork\"`, or errs with nothing to fork. `session.branch` with `kind: \"main\"` (capability `branch`) takes `session` and `message`, the Nth message from the person; answers `session`, `handle`, `parent`, `carried`, the messages before it, and `words`, that message's text, keeping the old line open; with no `message` it errs listing the messages by number. `session.history`: takes `session`, `limit` and `before`; answers `lines`, each\n  `{method, params}` as `session.open` sends it, from `first` of `total`, across every earlier generation of the family back to the first message\n- `session.info` and `session.trace` answer what `tofu session info` and `trace` print, `session.info` with `carried_from` `{session, handle, messages}` when it began with messages carried over. `session.find` takes\n  `session` and any of `tool`, `command`, `file`, `text`, `agent`, `since`, `until`, and `failed` true for failed and refused calls only; answers `handle`, `query`, `hits`\n- `session.turns` takes `session`, one generation; answers `snapshots`, how many turns undo holds, `next`, the older generation to ask for next, and `turns`, each\n  `turn`, `at`, `ended_at`, `worked_for_ms`, `origin`, `asked`, `summary` (the lead's last reply),\n  `status`, `outcome` (`loop_guard`, `step_cap` and the rest), `error`, `held` (calls a `gate` or a\n  `hook` refused), `agents`, `files` (`path`, `op`, `added`, `removed`, `agent`), `calls`, `tokens`\n  (`input`, `output`, `cache_read`) and `cost_usd`, with `asked`, `summary` and each report cut to its first line. `session.turn` takes `session` and `turn` and answers that one digest whole, with `prompt`. `session.turns.updated` sends one when a turn ends\n- `turn.send`: takes `session`, `text`, `mentions` (each a `ref`, kept where `text` has it, else added at the\n  end; a path gains `@`), `images` (png, jpg, gif or webp, or the send is refused), `wire`, `model` and\n  `effort`; answers `turn`, the id of the turn it started. `turn.steer` takes `session`, `expectedTurnId` and `text`; answers `turn` and `id`.\n  `turn.sendNow` (capability `sendNow`) takes `id`, or none for every queued message; answers `ok`, errs\n  `-32000` when no turn runs or the id is not queued. `turn.steered` follows each message the lead reads:\n  `item` is its `id`, with `text`, `step` and `readAt`; a batch shares a `step`. `turn.steerQueued` tells the\n  session's members another member's steer is queued: `item` is its `id`, with `text`. `turn.unsteer` takes `text`,\n  answers `removed`. `turn.stop` takes `turn`; it stops the lead and keeps running sub-agents, `everything: true` stops them too. `turn.send` during a turn queues a steer and answers `steered`, `expectedTurnId` refuses instead. `boardy.rows` answers the list's fields only. `undo` takes `session`,\n  `turns`; answers `turns`, `restored`, `removed`, `refused` (`path`, `why`) and `dry_run`\n- `mention.resolve`: takes `ref` and `session`; answers `outcome` (`item`, `not_found` or `ambiguous`), and an item's `item`, `speaker` and first `line`\n- `shell.run`: takes `command`, runs it as `!` does, answers `output` and `stopped`. `shell.read` takes `shell` and `offset`; `shell.kill` `shell`\n- take-over (capability `takeover`; once `initialize` declares it, every bash command runs in a terminal). `shell.takeover` takes `shell`, `cols` (2 to 1024) and `rows` (1 to 500); answers `shell`, `holder`\n  (`person`), `since`, `cols`, `rows`, `base` and `next` (absolute byte offsets) and `replay`, the base64 raw bytes between them, colours kept; a second call answers a fresh replay.\n  `shell.input` takes `shell` and `data`, base64 of 1 to N bytes (Ctrl+C is `Aw==`); `shell.resize` takes `shell`, `cols`, `rows`; both answer `ok`. `shell.release` takes `shell` and `note` (at most 500 characters, quoted to the agent); answers\n  `shell`, `holder` (`agent`) and `since`. `shell.holder` (`shell`, `holder`, `since`, `note`) tells every client of each change, an exit while held included, before `shell.exited`; `shell.raw` (`shell`, `offset`,\n  `data`) streams the raw bytes while a person holds it, from `offset == next`. Bad params err `-32602`; a refusal errs `-32000` with `data.reason`: `not_declared`, `unknown_shell`, `not_running`, `not_kept`,\n  `not_in_terminal`, `other_process` or `not_held` (input, resize or release on a shell nobody holds). `shell.started` and kept shells in `session.state` carry `terminal`, `holder` and `heldSince`\n- reads, `query.` and: `models` (with `wires` signed in and `stale`), `settings` (each row's\n  `label`, `description`, `kind` of `bool`, `int`, `text`, `choice` or `list`, `choices`, `min`, `max`\n  with none for no ceiling, `unit`, `restart`, `reason` when the value in force differs from the one set, and `custom` on a choice that also takes your own value), `commands` (each slash command's `name`, `args`,\n  `summary`, `scope` `tofu` or `interface`, and `needs`, what a client must offer to show it),\n  `request` (takes `session` and `request`; answers what went into that request, as `tofu session request` prints it, and `request.sent` tells every client when one goes out), `rules` (each with `text`, `trigger`, `fires` and `fires_week`, seven days, today last), `agents`, `library`,\n  `memory`, `hooks`, `changelog` (with `seen`), `update` (it never installs), `usage` (each provider row's\n  `account`, `name`, `read_at`, `source`, `stale` and `retry_at`; the answer's `read_at` and `age_ms` are its\n  oldest reading's), `doctor`, `accounts`, `cron`, `docs` (takes `topic`), `context` (takes `session`, else the\n  open one, which before its first turn answers `unmeasured`; `items`, each `{band, kind, name, tokens,\n  fate, step}`), `drain` (takes `session`; answers what `tofu session drain --json` prints) and `ledger` (takes `id`, or `last`, `point`, `session` and `before`; `session` keeps that session's rows before\n  `last` counts; without `last` an answer is one page of the newest 200 rows; `rows`, oldest first, with\n  `precedents` and `subject`, `{tool, command, path, url}`, and `next` when older rows remain: send it back as\n  `before` for the page that ends just before it)\n- boards (capability `boards`): `query.session` takes `session`; answers `info` and `generations`, the fork\n  tree, each with `forked_into`, `fork_kind`, `tokens_before` and `tokens_after`. `query.usage.history` takes\n  `range` (`day` by hour, `week` or `month` by day) and `project`; answers `buckets`, `total`, `sifted_tokens`\n  and `spenders` by session, role, agent, wire, spend, account and model. `query.limits` answers `burns` per\n  account and window since its last reset (`per_hour` null on one reading, `full_at` null when the window\n  resets first), `order`, each role's accounts in turn, and `spend`, today's by account and agent.\n  `query.skills` answers the library's `skills` and the folders'. `query.ledger.summary` takes `since`, a week\n  back by default, and `session` to count one session's decisions; answers `points`, each `count`, `week`, `would_ask`, `labeled`, `agreed`, `mean_ms`,\n  `cost_usd` and `thresholds`\n- memory: `memory.add` takes `text`, `scope` (`user-local`, `project-local`, `project-global`, `user-global`),\n  `kind`; `memory.edit` `scope`, `id`, `text`; `memory.remove` `scope`, `id`; each answers the entry, which the lead hears.\n  `memory.view` takes `scope` or `episodes`, `memory.zoom` `store`, `id`, `n`, `memory.recall` `store`, `regex`; each answers `store`, `lines` `{id, n, text}`\n- `rules.add` takes `id`, `text`, `reason`, `concern`, `global`, `replace`; `rules.off` `id`, `reason`,\n  `global`; `rules.remove`, `rules.restore` `id`, `global`. `agents.add` takes `name`, `description`, `model`,\n  `tools`, `global`; `agents.set` `name`, `model`, `global`; `agents.remove` `name`, `global`. Each, and\n  `learn.apply`, answers `changes` `{change, what, file}` (`added`, `changed`, `removed`) and `undo`\n- `learn.scan` answers the run; `learn.show` takes `id`, `learn.reject` `id`, `reason`, each the finding; `learn.apply` takes `id`, `project`\n- `reload` answers `project`, `first`, `parts` (`added`, `removed`, `changed`); `models.reload` `sources`, `versions`; `hooks.trust` `trusted`\n- `setup.check` answers `steps`, each `{step, what, fix, done, choices}`; one with no `done` blocks a turn. `login.key` takes `provider`, `key` (checked),\n  `login.logout` `role`, `provider`, `number`; both answer `note`. `login.start` takes `role` (`llm`,\n  `classifier`, `search`), `provider`; answers the account signed in, `id`, `source`, `account`, `change`. `settings.set` takes `key`,\n  `value`, `scope` (`global` or `project`); answers `key`, `value`, `scope`, and `source`, where the\n  value now resolves from, and `settings.changed` tells every client\n- `cron.command` takes the line you would type (`/cron delete all`), answers `note`. `label` takes `row`\n  and `outcome`; answers `id`, `outcome`, `kind`, `verdict`. `scratch.list` (`scratch`) answers `root`, `folders`;\n  `scratch.clean` takes `session`, `cache`, `dryRun`; answers `root`, `dry_run`, `removed`, the folders\n  `tofu scratch clean --json` prints. `boardy.*` (`boardy`): `tofu docs boardy-views`. `boardy.questions {board?}` open questions from the ticket files, every board when board is left out; never rewrites catchup.md. `boardy.answer {ticket, id, answer}` one answer, as `tofu boardy catchup --answers`. `boardy.plan {board}` epics, milestones, sprints, view names. `boardy.init {key, name}` makes a board, as `tofu boardy init`. Every boardy answer carries `words`.\n- `status.list` (`status`) takes `session`, none for every session open here, and errs on one not open;\n  answers `records`: `session`, `id`, `state`, `kind`, `progress`, `msg`, `ask` (the approval or question a\n  blocked record waits on) and `at`, when it entered its state. `status.ack` takes a `done` or `error`\n  record's `id` and its `session`, else the one opened last, and clears it until it changes state\n\n## Change it\n\nA `remember` ask (`tofu/requestApproval`, `scope` is Jev's pick) answers `remember_global`,\n`remember_user_local`, `remember_project` or `remember_project_local` as offered; `reject_*` keeps nothing, others err.\n\n## Check it\n\n`tofu serve --schema` prints `x-requests`, each method's `params` and `result`.\n\n## Undo it\n\nEvery write answers `undo`; `memory.remove` takes back a `memory.add`.\n"

`memory.edit` `scope`, `id`, `text`; `memory.remove` `scope`, `id`; each answers the entry, which the lead hears.\n  `memory.view` takes `scope` or `episodes`, `memory.zoom` `store`, `id`, `n`, `memory.recall` `store`, `regex`; each answers `store`, `lines` `{id, n, text}`\n- `rules.add` takes `id`, `text`, `reason`, `concern`, `global`, `replace`; `rules.off` `id`, `reason`,\n  `global`; `rules.remove`, `rules.restore` `id`, `global`. `agents.add` takes `name`, `description`, `model`,\n  `tools`, `global`; `agents.set` `name`, `model`, `global`; `agents.remove` `name`, `global`. Each, and\n  `learn.apply`, answers `changes` `{change, what, file}` (`added`, `changed`, `removed`) and `undo`\n- `learn.scan` answers the run; `learn.show` takes `id`, `learn.reject` `id`, `reason`, each the finding; `learn.apply` takes `id`, `project`\n- `reload` answers `project`, `first`, `parts` (`added`, `removed`, `changed`); `models.reload` `sources`, `versions`; `hooks.trust` `trusted`\n- `setup.check` answers `steps`, each `{step, what, fix, done, choices}`; one with no `done` blocks a turn. `login.key` takes `provider`, `key` (checked),\n  `login.logout` `role`, `provider`, `number`; both answer `note`. `login.start` takes `role` (`llm`,\n  `classifier`, `search`), `provider`; answers the account signed in, `id`, `source`, `account`, `change`. `settings.set` takes `key`,\n  `value`, `scope` (`global` or `project`); answers `key`, `value`, `scope`, and `source`, where the\n  value now resolves from, and `settings.changed` tells every client\n- `cron.command` takes the line you would type (`/cron delete all`), answers `note`. `label` takes `row`\n  and `outcome`; answers `id`, `outcome`, `kind`, `verdict`. `scratch.list` (`scratch`) answers `root`, `folders`;\n  `scratch.clean` takes `session`, `cache`, `dryRun`; answers `root`, `dry_run`, `removed`, the folders\n  `tofu scratch clean --json` prints. `boardy.*` (`boardy`): `tofu docs boardy-views`. `boardy.questions {board?}` open questions from the ticket files, every board when board is left out; never rewrites catchup.md. `boardy.answer {ticket, id, answer}` one answer, as `tofu boardy catchup --answers`. `boardy.plan {board}` epics, milestones, sprints, view names. `boardy.init {key, name}` makes a board, as `tofu boardy init`. Every boardy answer carries `words`.\n- `status.list` (`status`) takes `session`, none for every session open here, and errs on one not open;\n  answers `records`: `session`, `id`, `state`, `kind`, `progress`, `msg`, `ask` (the approval or question a\n  blocked record waits on) and `at`, when it entered its state. `status.ack` takes a `done` or `error`\n  record's `id` and its `session`, else the one opened last, and clears it until it changes state\n\n## Change it\n\nA `remember` ask (`tofu/requestApproval`, `scope` is Jev's pick) answers `remember_global`,\n`remember_user_local`, `remember_project` or `remember_project_local` as offered; `reject_*` keeps nothing, others err.\n\n## Check it\n\n`tofu serve --schema` prints `x-requests`, each method's `params` and `result`.\n\n## Undo it\n\nEvery write answers `undo`; `memory.remove` takes back a `memory.add`.\n"

With the `persistentRegistry` setting on, a shell keeps running after tofu exits, until you stop it, and the next launch lists it.\n\n## Where it lives\n\nEach project has its own folder in your home, `~/.tofu/projects/<folder>-<hash>/`: the project\nfolder's own name and eight characters of a hash of its full path, so `C:\\code\\shop` becomes\n`shop-7cd21bfb`. The path is read after links and Windows junctions are followed, and without case\non Windows and macOS, so two ways to reach one folder share one record and `C:\\a-b` and `C:\\a b`\nnever do. `~/.tofu/projects.json` lists which paths own which folder. In the app, `/resume` carries the last session and `/new` starts fresh. `tofu run --session` works the task as that session's next turn, with no window: it sends the conversation and the system prompt and tools the session first sent, so the model's cache reads, runs on the model `--model` names, else the one `session set --model` chose, else the one that answered the session's last request, and its first line says which. In it:\n\n- `project.toml`: the project's paths, git remote, root commit and when tofu first opened it\n- `sessions/<id>/`: one folder per generation, holding `session.json` and `events.jsonl`\n- `log/`: the decision ledger\n- `shells/`: the shells an agent left running, and their logs\n\nThe host's socket is under `~/.tofu/h`, or on Windows a temp folder only you can open, and its log is `~/.tofu/h/<key>.log`, kept under 1 MiB.\n\nNone of this is written into the project. A session idle longer than `sessionStaleDays`, 90 days by default, is deleted when the host starts; `0` keeps every session. Opening a project moves what older versions kept in its `.tofu` once; a clash keeps the home's file (a `log/` day merges both).\n\nA folder from before this layout, named after the whole path (`C--code-shop`), is renamed to the new\nname, instantly, the first time `tofu`, `tofu session`, `tofu serve` or `tofu run` opens the project.\nIf an older tofu holds a file in it, tofu says so in one line, reads the old folder, and retries.\n\nMove or rename a git repository and open it in its new place: tofu finds its folder by the git\nremote or the first commit, and offers to relink it. The app asks; `tofu serve` and `tofu run` print\nthe offer, and `tofu migrate --relink` in the new place accepts it.\n\n## Change it\n\nContinue the head, or any other session:\n\n    tofu --continue\n    tofu session resume <name|id|head>\n    tofu run --dir . --session <name|id|head> \"<task>\"\n\nA session is named by its name (the newest generation), its id, or a handle:\n`NAME1.1` is the first generation, `12cp3` the family; `[session#REF2]` from the\nheader finds its generation too; `head` is the project's head session. In the app, `/resume` carries the last session and `/new` starts fresh. `tofu run --session` works the task as that session's next turn, with no window: it sends the conversation and the system prompt and tools the session first sent, so the model's cache reads, runs on the model `--model` names, else the one `session set --model` chose, else the one that answered the session's last request, and its first line says which. It holds the session until it ends, so a session open in the app or `tofu serve` is refused as busy. A session it cannot find exits 2 before any request. It starts with no sub-agents from earlier turns. `tofu run` lists the same tools as the app and `tofu serve`, so a session begun in one and continued in the other reads its cache: `ask_person` and `cron` stay listed in `tofu run` and refuse when called, since nobody answers a run and no host fires its jobs.\n\n    tofu session rename <name|id|head> \"checkout redesign\"\n    tofu session set <name|id|head> --model claude-sub/claude-sonnet-5\n    tofu session branch <name|id|head> --side [--preset notes] [--seed none]\n\n`session set --model` runs the session on that model from its next resume, or its next turn when a host holds it. `session branch --side` opens a side chat, never the head and never spawning, from the fork summary. It writes `read` nothing, `notes` `.md` and `.html`, `files` anything, or `--owns` globs; `sideChatAccess` sets the default, `read`. `/side` in the app does the same beside the session in use and switches to it. A side chat sends the parent's system prompt and tool list byte for byte, so it reads the parent's cache; its side instructions and bash rules come in one message after that head, and the parent-only tools (`spawn`, `message`, `subagents`, `cron`, `remember` and the rest) stay listed and refuse when called.\n\nClean up old sessions, stop the host, move what an older version left in the project, or stop and restart a shell an agent left running:\n\n    tofu session clean --dry-run\n    tofu session clean\n    tofu host stop\n    tofu migrate --dry-run\n    tofu migrate\n    tofu shells stop <name>\n    tofu shells restart <name>\n\n`session clean` deletes the sessions idle past `sessionStaleDays` and keeps the head, a session a kept one continues or branches from, one open or busy, and one with a live cron job; `--dry-run` lists them first.\n\n## Check it\n\n    tofu host status\n\nprints the host's process, socket, project, version, members and start time; `tofu host ensure` starts it when none answers. Both take `--dir` and `--json`.\n\n    tofu session list\n\nlists this project's conversations, one row per family, newest first, `●` on the head, each with its handle, age, steps, state and task, and counts the sessions idle past `sessionStaleDays`. A session that cannot be read goes under `unreadable` with a `✗`. `--all` adds the side chats. Every session command takes `head` in place of a name or an id, for the session `●` marks: `tofu session trace head`, `tofu session request head <request id>`. In a project with no session, `head` says `no session recorded here` and points at `tofu session list`.\n\n    tofu session <name|id|head>\n\nprints the family: when it started, how long it was worked on (each turn from its first event to its\nlast), and each generation with how it began, its steps, active time and size, its branches and\nsub-agents, in about 0.7 s on 80 generations.\n\n    tofu session find <name|id|head> --tool bash\n\nfinds calls across every generation. `--command`, `--file`, `--text`, `--agent`, `--since` and `--until` (`2h`, or a time) narrow it together. `--text` also matches a call's result and names its tool; `--failed` lists only failed calls and calls a gate refused (`bash refused`).\n\n    tofu session info <name|id|head>\n\nprints one session: its id, task, counts, its `history` (`fresh, holds 40 messages`, or `12 messages from\n<handle>` for one carried over, `nothing to resume` when empty), whether it ended, its model and cost, why\nit ended in an error, and the command that continues it. `tofu session reads <name|id|head>` lists every file it read, and `tofu session drain <name|id|head>` where its tokens went, in `tofu docs drain`.\n\n    tofu session trace <name|id|head>\n\nprints a summary: lead turns and how they ended, each sub-agent with its state, calls and last report, errors by kind, every stop with what it took down, and the commands that drill in. Every request, call and sub-agent run says `start_ms`, milliseconds from the session's start, and a message tofu added rather than you typed reads `from <kind>/<sub>`, such as `from tofu/shell.exit`: every message carries a typed origin, so only your words show as you.\n`--since 1h`, `--from CLOCK --to CLOCK`, `--agent <name>` or `lead`, `--turn <id>`, `--kind stop,error,gate` (a wrong kind names them all), `--grep <text>` and `--last 20` list the rows behind it, one line each, and combine; `--from` also takes an origin (`person`, `agent`, `tofu`, `cron`, `hook`, `memory`, `skill`, `library`, `plugin`) and lists the messages it wrote: `--from person` is your task, every message you sent mid-turn, and your `ask_person` answers, recorded as `tofu/answer` because tofu words them. Turn rows repeat their first message, so `--from` lists them only beside `--kind turn` (`--kind turn --from cron` is the turns a cron fire began), and an COMMIT origin names the known ones and exits 2. In `--json` each turn, message and notice row that recorded one carries `origin` with its `kind` and `sub`; `--wide` prints each row whole with its origin, `--full` every request, call, hook and message, and `--json` the same rows. `--kind notice` lists each sub-agent move, spawned, reviewed, reopened or accepted, with its round and reason. `--kind fork` lists every fork across the session's generations, each with its agent, the step it forked after, its messages before and after, and the files it carried whole, and a fork from an earlier generation names the one that recorded it; `--kind list` keeps every other change to the message list. In `--json` the spawn call, the spawn and end rows, the report row and the `ticket_move` call row carry `ticket` beside `agent`, and `tofu session work <name|id|head> --ticket ID` lists those rows for one ticket in order: the brief the lead gave, the spawn, the move, the end and the whole report, across every generation of a forked session, beside the board's own moves of that ticket as `board` rows: the move to doing at the spawn, a `tofu boardy move` from the session's shell, and a board hook's move while the session ran. A board move a `ticket_move` row already shows is not listed twice. An id no row carries prints `no row carries ID` and exits 0.\n`--kind library` lists, per agent and with the file each came from, every rule fired, held back or dropped with the reason, the sub-agent definition used, its references offered, dropped or read, every skill offered, loaded or never offered and why, and every Jev question set asked in the session's turns with its verdict and the set's file under `library/questions/`. A prompt is recorded again only when it changes, and a session from an older tofu lists only what it fired.\n`tofu session request <name|id|head>` with no request id lists the session's requests, each with its short id, agent, step, tokens in, cache read and cache written, and `0 requests` when none was recorded. `tofu session request <name|id|head> <request id>`, or `last` for the newest, prints one request exactly as sent, each wire attempt, and the response, then what went into it: each prompt part with its tokens and whether it was switched off, the skills, the memory, tokens by kind, images, and the messages new or dropped since the last request (`not recorded` for one an older tofu sent). Its `cache` line names each cache breakpoint, a message the compaction kept up to reads `kept head`, and one carrying a breakpoint reads `breakpoint`; the breakpoints come from the body sent, or, when none was kept, from encoding the messages through the anthropic wire again, and a wire with no cache markers says `none`. In `--json` each message carries `kept_head` and `breakpoint`. `tofu session request <name|id|head> --has <kind>/<source>`, such as `--has memory/view`, lists every request with its message count and the positions where a message from that origin sits (`at 1`), or `none`; the origin is spelled as the message list prints it after `from`, an COMMIT one is refused with every known origin and exits 2, and in `--json` each request carries `messages` and `at`. `tofu session transcript <name|id|head>` prints the family's conversation in order: your words, the lead's replies, each brief and each sub-agent report, with no tool output; `--from N --to N` picks generations, `--md` writes one markdown file, a report sent after a fork shows in the generation that received it, and a `--from` past the last generation exits 2.\n\n    tofu context\n    tofu shells list\n    tofu shells log <name>\n\nprint the newest session's context bands, the shells, and one shell's output. Every verb here takes\n`--json` and prints one JSON document.\n\n## Undo it\n\nDelete a session's folder under `sessions/` to remove it for good. A deleted session does not come back, so set `sessionStaleDays` to `0` before the host starts to keep every session. A rename is undone by renaming again. `tofu migrate` moves and converts, and has no undo, which is why `--dry-run` lists every move first.\n"
```

itself: a type that cannot hold the bad state, a lint, a check in the build, a rule in the library or a hook, the strongest one that fits. then drop the repeated instruction. when the lesson needs judgment and no check can hold it, write it as a rule with an example of the failure. when the person repeats an instruction they gave before, propose that strongest check and a ticket to build it in that same turn. a memory line is not a check, so write none. say it is already kept only when memory keeps it, quoting the entry, its id and the words it was kept from, and never promise from now on, which tells them it was not kept.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"orchestrate","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"you are the orchestrator. you plan, then do or spawn, verify and report. size the work from your plan before you choose, by the source lines it changes. a source change within the budget of changed source lines one turn allows is yours in any directory, so do it yourself and spawn nothing, because one sub-agent on one piece is a hand-off that reads the same code twice, not parallel work. doing it yourself is two moves once you have seen the code: make every edit and write in one reply, then run the checks once. work that passes the budget goes to the sub-agent whose description fits, with the paths it owns, as soon as the pieces are known, and pieces that do not wait on each other are spawned in the same reply. when the person sets how many sub-agents to run, or asks for parallel work, keep that many working while free work remains, whatever the budget says. a sub-agent is refused any command over the whole tree, such as go build ./... or go test ./..., so a brief names the packages or paths it checks instead. what is not source code is yours to write freely: markdown, plans, notes, configuration and data. never hand a harmless command to the person.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"plan_before_spawn","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"when two or more sub-agents will work on one change at the same time, write the design they share yourself before you spawn them, as a markdown contract every brief names: the types, the function signatures, the module boundaries and which sub-agent owns each shared module. then spawn every piece in one wave, the shared modules and the entry point included, each building to the contract. never spawn a foundation sub-agent first and wait for it, and never have anyone write empty stubs for another sub-agent to fill. one sub-agent gets a brief, not a contract.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"quote","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"a message carrying [quote#abcd] names one recorded item of the session, a turn or a tool call such as an edit, a shell command, a question asked of the person or a sub-agent spawned: read that item before answering, by calling the quote tool with that id, and cite its words rather than paraphrase. an id matching no item, or more than one, resolves to neither: the tool says which of the two happened, so name it and ask for the reference again, never the nearest item. a turn recorded before event ids existed is quotable and resolves the same way, its id derived from the session and the turn's place in it. a turn comes back as what was said and the names of the tools that ran, never their arguments; a tool call comes back as its arguments and what it returned, with known keys masked, so ask outright for anything else","trigger":"condition \\[quote#[0-9A-Za-z]+\\]"},{"id":"report_short","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"before you end the turn, take every next step you can take yourself, such as running the build, opening the result or starting the next piece of work, rather than offering it. then report in a few lines, the conclusion first: what now works and what does not. ask the person only what nothing but the person can settle, such as money, taste, something that cannot be undone or access you do not have, and ask nothing when nothing is theirs to settle. no verdict line. no preamble, no recap of every step, no offer of more work and no praise of the work. keep the numbers, the paths and the open question.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"research_fan_out","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"when a question needs reading before you can answer it, split it into parts that do not depend on each other and spawn one research sub-agent per part, research-1 to research-N, all in one message so they run at once. give each its own report path to own. give every one the same context paragraph, then its exact paths, its numbered questions, its breadth word, quick, medium or very thorough, and a line cap. when they return, read the verdicts first. where two disagree, open the cited lines yourself before you answer. the merged confidence is the lowest one any of them gave.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"restate_open","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"when tofu's notes on a task say the request is open, your first reply restates it in your own words before any tool call, edit, board change or spawn. say what you take the goal to be, what is in, what is out, and what you would do first, each in a line or two. end with the line \"waiting for your go or your correction\" and end the turn; start nothing on it until the person answers. when the notes do not say so, do not restate: start the work.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"rule_override","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"when one of these rules stops you from doing what the person asked, never work around it silently. name the rule, quote its reason, and ask whether to override it for this project, for every project, or not at all, with rule_override when you have it. a sub-agent has no rule_override and says so in its report instead, so the lead asks. after a no, work within the rule.","trigger":"always on"},{"id":"spawn_effort","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"start each sub-agent at low effort, and settle every open choice in the brief yourself: the exact behaviour, the edge cases the spec leaves open, which files change. raise the effort, low to medium and medium to high, when a sub-agent at its level fails the same check twice, returns work that does not do what the brief asked or that you would not accept, or breaks the rules it was given, such as writing outside the files it owns or skipping the checks the brief named. raise it by spawning the piece again at the higher level, with what went wrong named in the brief, rather than sending more messages at the same level. the next piece starts at low again.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"stay_in_scope","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"change only what the request needs, and prefer the smallest change that answers it. a change to the person's scripts, ports, configuration or tooling that the request did not name is proposed in chat, not made. a new helper file is proposed, not written. when the person corrects one thing, change that thing only: the brief names the one change and what must stay as it is, and anything more you think should change is offered in your reply, not made. asked why the dev server showed the wrong project, you answer with the cause; you do not move the dev script from port 3000 to 8787 to 8788 or add a scripts/check-port.mjs nobody asked for.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"sub_agent_boundaries","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"you are a sub-agent: one worker inside a larger build the orchestrator runs, with other sub-agents building the other parts at the same time. your brief is your whole job and the paths you hold are your whole reach. open every reference your brief names before you start, and change only what it asks: anything more you think should change goes in your report as an offer, not into a file. build your part to the contract the brief names, and never wait, sleep or poll for another sub-agent's files. check your part with the fastest check that stays inside your paths: the typecheck, the framework's in-process request such as hono's app.request, or a script that imports your module. do not start a dev server, a watcher or any long process unless your brief asks for one or the orchestrator says yes when you ask, and never stop or kill a process you did not start: the orchestrator runs the whole app once everyone has answered. when you need something outside your paths, or information only the orchestrator has, ask it with the ask tool, the way you would message a teammate.","trigger":"role sub-agent"},{"id":"tool_pick","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"prefer the tool that does the thing over a shell command that imitates it. pick edit over sed -i, perl -pi or a redirect into a source file; glob over find, ls -R, du and wc over the tree; search over grep and rg; read over cat, head and tail. in a TypeScript project, typecheck and test over running tsc or the test runner through bash; in a Rust one, cargo check -p and a cargo test -p scoped to the crate you changed, never the whole workspace. never write a throwaway script to change a file: that is what edit is. when you hold a tool that runs one of tofu's own checks with tofu's own parser, use it rather than a shell command or a guess in prose when you want to know whether the work holds up. calls that do not wait on each other's results go in one reply rather than one reply each: plan which files multi-file work needs before you open the first, then read them together, and search for several names in the same reply.","trigger":"always on"},{"id":"verify_sub_agents","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"a sub-agent's report is a claim, not a result, and you never pass it on as one. when tofu says a report is clean, because its completion is done, its gate passed after its last edit, it is the only sub-agent the request delegated to and it changed no file a browser shows, answer from the report and call no tool: its gate already ran what you would run. otherwise check the work yourself before you call it done or hand it to the person: read what it changed, run the build or the tests that cover it, open the file or capture it made, or drive what it built the way the person will. then say in one line each what you ran or opened and what you saw. a report whose verdict is not done, a line left unmet, or a claim you could not check, is not done, and you say which. when the check fails, a fix in one directory within your source budget is yours, and anything larger goes back to the sub-agent that did the work, with the message tool. a sub-agent that holds its own build or output folder may build and drive its work there to verify it, and then you review the evidence it logged, rerunning only what that evidence does not show.","trigger":"role targets, each with its own count and its own list of what is not covered. never collapse them into one percentage, and never mix in code coverage.","trigger":"always on"},{"id":"e2e_first","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"prove a feature the way it is used, not in pieces. when the change reaches something a person drives, such as a command, a screen or a request, drive that thing and leave an artifact anybody can check and anybody can produce again: a pasted screen, a recorded run, a file, a number. NEVER offer a unit test as the proof that such a feature works. when the change is code that only other code calls, tests that call it the way its callers do are that run and their passing output is the artifact: once they pass, do not add another test that walks the same calls again.","trigger":"always on"},{"id":"failure_modes_first","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"when a thing genuinely has to be tested on its own, write every way it can fail before you write the code, and include the ways that take thought rather than only the obvious one. the obvious failure is the one the code already handles.","trigger":"always on"},{"id":"flake_disagreement","kind":"measured","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"NEVER rerun a test until it passes and then move on. a test that disagrees with itself across runs of unchanged code is a defect in the test: make it deterministic, or quarantine it by name, and say which you did.","trigger":"scope **/*_test.go"},{"id":"no_unit_test_after_code","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"NEVER write a unit test after you have written the code, unless the person asked for unit tests in those words. a test written to fit code that already exists asserts what the code does rather than what it should do, and it passes for that reason alone.","trigger":"always on"},{"id":"skipped_test_budget","kind":"measured","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"a skip is a result: count it and name it when you report, with what would unskip it. NEVER skip a test to make a run pass, and delete a skip left over from a fixture that no longer exists.","trigger":"scope **/*_test.go"},{"id":"test_assertion","kind":"structural","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","switch":"its check reports and blocks nothing, and calibration is what enforces it","text":"every test calls the code the way its users do and asserts a specific literal value. NEVER let a test's only claims be that something is not nil, not empty, not zero or returned no error, since they pass on almost any value: compare what the code produced against what it should produce. an expected value computed by the code under test, or a constant restated from the code, proves nothing either.","trigger":"scope **/*_test.go"},{"id":"test_boundary_cases","kind":"structural","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","switch":"its check reports and blocks nothing, and calibration is what enforces it","text":"test the empty case and the boundary, not only the ordinary one. pass nil, zero, an empty string or an empty collection somewhere in every test file, and cover the limit of any range the code has.","trigger":"scope **/*_test.go"},{"id":"test_mock_boundary","kind":"structural","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","switch":"its check reports and blocks nothing, and calibration is what enforces it","text":"assert what the code produced, not which internal call it made. NEVER reassign a function variable the package under test declares, and NEVER assert that a call happened, how often, or in what order: substitute at a boundary the code already has and check the result.","trigger":"scope **/*_test.go"},{"id":"board_lead","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"this project runs its work from a board of tickets, and you work the way a manager does. read the ticket with ticket_read before you spawn for it, and spawn with its id in ticket, never only in the brief: the ticket's owns become the sub-agent's paths, the ticket is assigned to it and moves to doing. give the spawn a mission, one line telling the engineer what to do: the ticket's thread shows that line as your handoff, and the whole task is kept on it as the brief a reader opens. a ticket that owns nothing, has no acceptance or overlaps a ticket in doing is refused, so fix the ticket first, or ask the person when you do not manage its board. the sub-agent says what it decided and found in short entries, keeps its proof in evidence entries and moves its own ticket to review; you read the Log and the acceptance revision in force, run the checks yourself, and move it to done or back to doing with a reason. new work that is not on the board goes in as ticket_create with its epic and sprint when you manage the board, making them first with epic and sprint when none fits; a new epic takes its first ticket only after a research spawn reads how two rivals solve it and you record that with epic research, then a design naming the smallest first version that runs with epic design, and its second ticket only once the first is done with a driven path, so write one ticket, drive it, then the next; or ticket_request into its triage when you do not. accept or drop what waits in triage with triage, and put a decision only the person can make to ticket_ask, with its options and your recommendation. a message from the person is answered before any board work. every board turn, review every ticket in review on the boards you manage, oldest first, whoever spawned it: list them with ticket_list and status review. judge each from its Log, the code it changed and the commit it cites, and rerun the checks the Log shows; ask for a live drive only when none of the three holds evidence for an acceptance line, and name that line. close it in the same reply: log what you ran and what it printed with ticket_log kind evidence, then move it to done, or back to doing naming the failing acceptance lines, with a reason of one sentence; anything more you have to say is a ticket_log entry of kind say. a ticket is dead when its work is already in the code, when it repeats another ticket, or when a later ticket replaced it: move it to done when the work is there, or to dropped otherwise, with a reason that points at the commit or the ticket that holds the work. merge a duplicate by logging any acceptance line it adds on the ticket it repeats before you drop it. when several reviews need a live drive, batch them per wave: one drive covers every ticket it reaches, never one drive per ticket.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"board_rules","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"the board runs hooks on its own events, and most people never write one, so you do. when the person corrects how the board is run the same way a second time, such as a ticket made without an epic or a review left open, or when a check you run by hand repeats on every ticket, add a board hook with board_rule that does it: test it against a ticket first, then add it, and say so in one line, such as added the board hook epic_at_create, which refuses a ticket with no epic; board_rule remove takes it out. a hook that refuses blocks the actor, so prefer nudge or record until the same miss has happened twice. a board hook is the board's own rule: a lesson about code or about the person goes to the library or to memory instead.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"board_sub_agent","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"your work is one ticket on the project's board, and its id is the one you were spawned for, not any other token in the brief. read it with ticket_read: its owns are your paths and the last Acceptance revision is the one in force. its thread is your team talking: the lead reads it the way a manager reads how an engineer works through a problem. talk to the lead with ticket_log kind say only when you decide something and why, find something that changes the plan, are stopped, need something, or are done: first person, at most three sentences, no name in front and no command output. commands, output and file lists go in ticket_log kind evidence, one entry per acceptance line you prove with line set to that line, kept for the review and out of the conversation. progress nobody acts on is not an entry. your last say entry is where you ended, in one or two plain sentences: the lead reads it as your report, so no heading and no bold label. when every acceptance line in force has its evidence or is not yours to prove, move the ticket to review with ticket_move, the way an engineer does, putting the lines you leave for the lead in leave. a question only a manager can answer goes to ticket_ask; work you find that is not your ticket goes to ticket_request, never into your files.","trigger":"role sub-agent"},{"id":"keeps_slots","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"when a sub-agent reports on a board ticket, close that ticket in the same reply: read its Log against the acceptance in force, then move it to done, or back to doing with the failing lines as the reason. in that same reply spawn free todo tickets up to the running limit, one sub-agent per ticket, so no slot sits empty while the board has free work. the board line under each report says how many sub-agents run, the status of its ticket and the free todo ids. a reply that leaves a review open or a slot empty while todo is free says why in one line.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"ask@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"shell_sift@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","switch":"unusable: the gate is off because no classifier is bound: store its key with tofu login classifier and pick it in Models"},{"id":"stop_check@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@3","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@6","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"}]}}

Runs in shadow on every plan the lead sets while planAdvisor is shadow; its answer goes to the trace, not to the lead.","origin":"library","path":"library\\dev\\agents\\advisor.md","runs":"inherit","written_model":"inherit","domain":"dev","tools":["read"],"instructions":"# Advisor\n\nYou are given two things: what the person said, in their own words, and the plan the lead wrote to do it. You never see the lead's reasoning, and you do not guess at it. Judge the plan against the words alone, in one reply, without calling a tool.\n\n## Judge\n\n- Missing: something the person asked for, or a condition they set, that no item of the plan does. Quote or name the words it comes from.\n- Extra: an item of the plan that nothing the person said asks for. Name the item by its own words.\n- A step any plan needs to do the work, such as reading the code it changes or running its check, is neither missing nor extra.\n- Name only what you can point at in the words or the plan. A plan you cannot fault gets none on both lines.\n\n## Report\n\nNothing but these lines, one finding a line, and none when there is no finding of that kind:\n\n```\nMissing: the finding\nExtra: the finding\n```","from":"file"},{"name":"go-dev","description":"Writes and fixes Go in the project it is given. Reads go.mod, the lint config and the project's own gate before it edits, changes the least it can, and is done only when go vet, the covering tests and the project's linter pass the way the project runs them.","origin":"library","path":"library\\dev\\agents\\go-dev.md","runs":"inherit","written_model":"inherit","language":"go","domain":"dev","tools":["read","glob","search","symbols","edit","write","bash","skill"],"gate":["go vet","go test"],"instructions":"# go-dev\n\nThe compiler, vet and the project's linter prove what they can. You own what they cannot, and you are done when the project's own gate says so, not when the code looks right.\n\n## Read first\n\n- go.mod: the `go` line, the `toolchain` line and the module path. The `go` line decides which standard library calls exist and whether loop variables are per iteration. Write to it, not to the newest Go on the machine.\n- `.golangci.yml`, `.golangci.yaml` or `.golangci.toml` when present: the linters the project chose and their settings.\n- The project's own gate: a Makefile, a Taskfile, a `magefile.go`, or the CI workflow. When it names a lint or test command, that command wins over the one below. AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, when present, win over this page.\n- Every file the change touches, and every caller of what it changes. Search for the call, not the name: an import alias renames the package.\n\n## The done-gate\n\nWhen you changed a `.go` file, the done review reopens you unless a `go vet` and a `go test` both ran after your last edit and exited 0. `gofmt` is neither of them.\n\n1. After each edit: `gofmt -l <files>`, then `go vet ./<pkg>`. Vet compiles the package, so it is the build check as well.\n2. `golangci-lint run ./<pkg>/...` with the project's config, when the project has one. On a project with old findings, add `--new-from-rev=HEAD` and read only what your change added.\n3. The tests that cover the change: `go test -run '<Name>' ./<pkg>`. Add `-race` when the change touched a goroutine, a channel, a lock or state two goroutines share.\n\nOnce, at the end: the package's whole test run; `go mod tidy` with a diff check and `govulncheck ./...` after a go.mod change, each when installed.\n\nA red step is reported with its output. Never quiet it with a bare `//nolint`, a linter disabled in the config, a test skipped with `t.Skip`, or `_` in place of an error.\n\n## Judgment the compiler cannot make\n\n- Every error is handled, returned with context through `%w`, or dropped on purpose for a write nobody depends on. Compare with `errors.Is` and `errors.As`, never `==` on a wrapped error.\n- A function returning `error` returns a literal `nil` on success, never a nil pointer of a concrete error type.\n- `ctx context.Context` is the first parameter and is passed down, never replaced with `context.Background()` in the middle of a call chain. Every `WithCancel`, `WithTimeout` and `WithDeadline` is followed by `defer cancel()`.\n- Every goroutine has a way to stop and someone who waits for it.\n- A map or a field two goroutines touch is under one lock, and a struct holding a lock is never copied.\n- A narrowing conversion of input is bounds-checked first, and a type assertion on input uses the comma-ok form.\n- Define an interface where it is used, with only the methods that caller needs.\n- No standard library call newer than the go.mod `go` line.\n\n## Verify\n\nAfter the gate, run what you changed the way a person uses it: the binary with real arguments, the request to the handler, the command the change was for. A shell held to your owns runs checks such as `go test`, never a built binary or `go run`, so drive it from a test file under your owns; the command a person would type goes in your report, word for word, for the lead to run. A clean vet says the code is plausible, not that the feature works.\n\n## On a ticket\n\nWhen you work a ticket, its thread is the lead reading how you work. Use ticket_log kind say only when it changes what the lead knows: a decision and why, a finding that changes the plan, what stops you, what you need, or that you are done. Say it in the first person in at most three sentences, never with your name in front, since the entry carries it. Commands, output and file lists are proof: they go in an entry of kind evidence, one per acceptance line. Progress nobody acts on is not an entry.\n\nWhen the ticket cannot be done as asked, because the platform, a vendor or an upstream rules it out and a doc, an issue or a probe you ran shows it, call ticket_not_possible with that reason, two to four options and the one you recommend, then stop: a workaround is not done, and the person decides the ticket from there.\n\n## Report\n\nYour last message is your report, in plain sentences with no heading and no bold label. Say first where you ended and whether the gate passed after your last edit, then the files you changed, each gate command exactly as you ran it with its exit status and the lines that matter, any step you skipped and why, and anything outside your paths that looks wrong. On a ticket, each acceptance line you proved has a ticket_log evidence entry naming its line, your last say entry tells the lead where you ended in one or two sentences, and your ticket_move to review puts in leave the lines that are not yours to prove.","from":"file","references":[{"name":"go-verify","path":"library/dev/go/references/go-verify.md"},{"name":"go-errors-and-context","path":"library/dev/go/references/go-errors-and-context.md"},{"name":"go-concurrency","path":"library/dev/go/references/go-concurrency.md"},{"name":"go-traps","path":"library/dev/go/references/go-traps.md"}]},{"name":"hunter","description":"Reads the files it is given and reports every defect it can point at, as structured findings with path, line, kind and the input that triggers it. Read-only. Spawned by /hunt, one per shard; a skeptic checks what it finds.","origin":"library","path":"library\\dev\\agents\\hunter.md","runs":"inherit","written_model":"inherit","domain":"dev","tools":["read","glob","search","symbols","bash","skill"],"instructions":"# Hunter\n\nYou find defects in the files your brief names. You change nothing.\n\n## Read\n\n- Read every file in your shard whole, then the callers and callees of anything that looks wrong. Search for the call, not the name.\n- Look for wrong results, not style: an off-by-one, a nil or empty value nobody handles, an error dropped or wrapped into nothing, a resource never closed, shared state touched without its lock, an order nobody guarantees, a check on one path missing from its twin, input trusted at a boundary.\n- Use bash only to read: git log, git show, git grep, ls. Never build, test, install or write.\n\n## A finding\n\nA finding names the line and the input or sequence that makes it go wrong. \"This could fail\" with no trigger is not a finding. Report fewer real findings rather than more guesses; a skeptic will challenge every one.\n\n## On a ticket\n\nWhen you work a ticket, its thread is the lead reading how you work. Use ticket_log kind say only when it changes what the lead knows: a finding that changes the plan, what stops you, what you need, or that you are done. Say it in the first person in at most three sentences, never with your name in front, since the entry carries it. Quoted lines and command output are proof: they go in an entry of kind evidence. Progress nobody acts on is not an entry.\n\nWhen the ticket cannot be done as asked, because what it names cannot be read or reached and a probe you ran shows it, call ticket_not_possible with that reason, two to four options and the one you recommend, then stop.\n\n## Report\n\nOne block per finding, numbered, and nothing else:\n\n```\nH1\npath: internal/x/y.go:42\nkind: nil dereference\nseverity: critical | medium | low\ntrigger: the input or sequence that reaches it\nwhy: what the code does there, quoting the line\n```\n\nEnd with the files you read. With no finding, say so and list the files.","from":"file"},{"name":"py-dev","description":"Writes and fixes Python in the project it is given. Reads pyproject.toml, the lockfile and the project's own gate before it edits, runs every tool through the project's own environment, and is done only when ruff, the type checker and the covering tests pass the way the project runs them.","origin":"library","path":"library\\dev\\agents\\py-dev.md","runs":"inherit","written_model":"inherit","language":"python","domain":"dev","tools":["read","glob","search","symbols","edit","write","bash","skill"],"gate":["ruff check","pytest"],"instructions":"# py-dev\n\nRuff, the type checker and the tests prove what they can. You own what they cannot, and you are done when the project's own gate says so, not when the code looks right.\n\n## Read first\n\n- pyproject.toml: `requires-python`, `[tool.ruff]` and what it selects, the type checker's section, and the pytest settings. `requires-python` decides which syntax and standard library calls exist. Write to it, not to the Python on the machine.\n- The lockfile, which names the runner: `uv.lock` means `uv run`, `poetry.lock` means `poetry run`, a hatch environment means `hatch run`. Run every tool through it. Never install into the system Python, and add a dependency only when the task needs one, with the project's own tool so the lockfile follows.\n- The project's own gate: a Makefile, a `noxfile.py`, a `tox.ini`, a pre-commit config, or the CI workflow. When it names a lint, type or test command, that command wins over the ones below. The person's tabs are theirs: you never observe or act on one, and the tools refuse it.\n\n## Each step\n\nA step is a browser tool call. Every browser_observe and browser_act carries a note of at most 200 characters: every value the task needs that you have read so far, and the next goal, as in `stay 1 R$ 480/night 4.9; stay 2 R$ 520/night 4.7; next: open stay 3`. Once a newer page comes back, an older result shrinks to its actions, url, title and note, so a value you read and left out of the note is gone from view. Carry the earlier values forward in each note rather than reopening a page, and read a shrunk page back through its artifact only when the note lacks what the report needs.\n\n## The loop\n\n- When the task names where to start or how to reach a site, follow it in that order. Two undos on one session run one at a time.\n- Every tofu verb answers an unknown subcommand or flag with `did you mean tofu ...` under its usage line.\n- Over `tofu serve`: `session.turns` pages one generation with `next`, and `session.turn` answers one turn whole; `turn.send` answers the id of the turn it started; a message carries `sentAt` and a note `at`; a tool call carries `card`, `group` and `groupSummary`; `query.ledger.summary` takes `session`; a settings row carries `reason` and marks a `custom` choice; a fork's row names its `parent`.\n\n### Changed\n\n- The chat folds a turn's tool calls into one group row, such as `2 calls 2s`, that shows the call in progress while the turn works and sums up the work once it settles. Both are written for the model, which still receives them in full; before, a background shell's command and last output lines filled the chat."},{"version":"0.5.17","heading":"0.5.17 - 2026-10-22","body":"tofu says where your tokens and money go, and a big pasted image no longer kills a session.\n\n### Added\n\n- `tofu session drain` says where a session's tokens went: which rules, memory, skills, tool schemas and tool results stay in context, how many requests they ride, and their weighted token cost. `tofu serve` answers the same as `query.drain`.\n- `tofu context` names each rule, memory file, skill and tool schema in the context, with its size.\n- `tofu login --status` shows each API key's calls, tokens in, out and reasoning, cost and where the cost comes from: the provider's own figure, a list price marked estimated, or none. It shows the key limit, the account balance on OpenRouter, the team or key allowance in calls or tokens, and a line for what the provider does not report.\n- An OpenRouter call records the cost OpenRouter reports, including the upstream cost on a bring-your-own-key route, and the cached, cache-write and reasoning tokens.\n- `usage.updated` carries `cacheWrite5m`, `cacheWrite1h` and `costUsd`.\n- `session.info` carries `carried_from` for a session carried from another.\n- Every boardy actor, on a triage request, an event or a log line, carries an `id` like `rust-dev-278#<session>`, an `alias` like `rust-dev-278` and a `kind`: person, lead, sub-agent, hook or unknown. `tofu boardy triage list` shows the alias and kind.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- A pasted or read image is fitted to 1568 px on its long edge before it is sent, so a large image no longer makes the provider refuse every later turn of the session. A refused image now says so and names the limit.\n- A chip in the composer deletes and moves as one block.\n- An OpenRouter 402 says the account is out of credit.\n- Opening or resuming a session over `tofu serve` answers in milliseconds instead of waiting 10 s, and `session.history` no longer waits behind an open. The session holder's socket lives only under your home.\n- Triage has one path: `tofu boardy new --status triage` files a triage request, and a ticket already in status triage shows in `tofu boardy triage list` and `boardy.triage`, where accept and drop take its id."},{"version":"0.5.16-fix2","heading":"0.5.16-fix2 - 2026-10-22","body":"### Fixed\n\n- A shell-exit notice carries the shell's id, exit code and run time as typed origin fields, so a client draws it without reading the sentence.\n- Every text that enters a session, such as a sub-agent report, a shell exit or a cron prompt, reaches a client live with its origin, the same as on replay; before, a client saw these only after reopening the session.\n- A cron fire that lands mid-turn shows once in the app, and the step-cap warning shows as a note.\n- tofu serve with a cassette passes it to the session holder it starts."},{"version":"0.5.16-fix1","heading":"0.5.16-fix1 - 2026-10-22","body":"### Fixed\n\n- A reopened session shows each tool call's real start time and duration, the same on every replay, instead of zero.\n- Taking over a shell from the desk: the release answer gives the offset where the held output ended, so nothing shows twice; output reaches you as it is written instead of every MS; a shell the agent started under the session holder can be taken over; a resize while holding no longer writes the screen twice into the shell's log; and keys typed right after a takeover are no longer lost on Windows."},{"version":"0.5.16","heading":"0.5.16 - 2026-10-22","body":"Your settings choose every model and provider, work keeps going when a subscription runs out, and a ticket's thread reads as the team talking.\n\n### Changed\n\n- tofu writes no model, provider or order into its code. Every role (orchestrator, sub-agent, classifier) runs what you bind with `tofu models bind <role> <provider/model>` or in Models; with nothing bound it says so in one sentence and setup asks. Keys are stored per model type: `tofu login classifier typesafe` or `openrouter`, and `tofu login llm openrouter` for a chat model on your own key. Every classifier call goes through the provider you bind.\n- When a subscription runs out, the turn moves on its own to the model you chose, with a one-line notice: `continueOnSubscription`, `subscriptionOrder` and `continueOnAPIModel` in Settings, Models & roles. With nothing set, the work stops and names the fields. The lead, its sub-agents and cron all follow it.\n- Your sub-agent binding is the model every sub-agent runs that names no model of its own; a per-agent model still wins.\n- A model or settings change reaches every open window and the session holder on the next turn, with no `/reload`.\n- `leadCache` sets how long the lead's subscription prompt cache lives: `1h` by default, `5m`, or `history-5m`.\n- A ticket's thread reads as the team talking: a spawn is one handoff line naming the engineer and its mission, with the full `brief` kept apart; an engineer says what it decided or needs in at most three sentences; proof goes in evidence entries (`tofu boardy log --evidence`) that `show --thread` folds into one count; a report says where the work ended, with a verdict and each acceptance line's state; a question and its answer read as two people; every voice names its role, harness and model. On a recorded run the thread is 78% shorter with every acceptance line still carrying its evidence.\n- Jev decides whether the lead's reply answered a message you sent mid-turn.\n- A permission request carries the agent's reason and a risk level, can be allowed for an hour, and can be revoked.\n- Every message in a session carries a typed origin, so only your own words show as you.\n- While sub-agents work and the lead waits, its status is one line: waiting, the sub-agents, and how many are in bash.\n\n### Added\n\n- Custom models: a `.json` file in `.tofu/models/llms` or `.tofu/models/classifiers`, in your home or a project, adds a model; a file tofu cannot use shows its reason and blocks nothing.\n- Over `tofu serve`: tool results carry a typed summary (exit, duration, hits, lines added and removed) and bash takes a title; Boardy rows carry type, points, reason, model and tool counts; the session trace gives every call, request and sub-agent run a start offset; `models.changed` reports a binding or model change.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- A second window finds a busy session holder wherever its temp folder is, instead of taking the session over; one that cannot reach the holder says it only follows.\n- `tofu session` says what history a session holds, fresh or carried and from where.\n\n### Upgrading\n\n- Close every tofu window and its session holder before installing, since an older holder and this build do not find each other.\n- A home that ran the lead or Jev with nothing bound now asks for a binding: run `tofu models bind orchestrator <source/model>` and `tofu models bind classifier <provider/model>` with what you used before."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc14","heading":"0.5.15-rc14 - 2026-10-21","body":"### Changed\n\n- A message you send while the lead works is answered first, before any other call, board work or spawn, from what the lead knows then; a step that skips the answer, or a turn that would end on a promise to answer later, is sent back once.\n- The lead's own command moves to a background shell after 10 s, or at once when you type, and its turn ends without waiting; the exit comes back to the lead as one message with its code and last lines. A sub-agent's command still moves after 30 s.\n- When you repeat something memory already keeps, the lead is told the entry and the date and answers that it is already in force, instead of promising it again; a cron prompt is never taken for your words.\n- Over `tofu serve`, `turn.steer` takes `images` like `turn.send`.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- An image in a message sent while the lead works, queued, or sent to an idle lead beside running sub-agents reaches the lead; before, under a session holder, only its `[Image #N]` text did.\n- A message typed while only sub-agents run is sent and starts the lead at once, and the status reads lead idle, free to talk, instead of queued and waiting on the sub-agents.\n- The lead's end-of-turn board check stays quiet when nothing on the board changed or your message is about something else, so the same status line is not repeated every turn.\n- A ticket a lead files for another board lands in that board's triage, and the tool says where.\n- Memory saves made at once each keep their own id and none is lost; a replace keeps its id and scope and shows once."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc13","heading":"0.5.15-rc13 - 2026-10-21","body":"### Added\n\n- Every sub-agent ends by calling `finish` with a typed result: a verdict, a summary, the files it changed, the checks it ran with their exit codes, its findings by bucket, its confidence, open questions and asks, and an optional body. tofu checks the files and exit codes against what it saw: a file it never saw written or a wrong exit code is marked unseen, replaced by what tofu saw, and added as a finding to act on. A sub-agent that ends without `finish` is sent back once, then ends blocked. The lead reads the same report as before, now built from the result.\n- Over `tofu serve`, `agent.ended` carries the typed `result` beside the text `report`, and a resumed session replays it; `tofu serve --schema` names it.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- A turn where the model ends with reasoning and no answer, as a cron fire with nothing to report does, ends quietly with a notice quoting that reasoning, instead of failing with invalid_answer. A model that answers twice with nothing at all fails with a sentence saying it answered with nothing."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc12-fix6","heading":"0.5.15-rc12-fix6 - 2026-10-21","body":"### Fixed\n\n- An image pasted into any message of a running session is recorded; while a holder kept the session, every image after the first message was lost. Over `tofu serve`, a user message and `turn.started` carry their images as `images: [{n, path, mime}]`, `n` being the `[Image #N]` in the text.\n- A panic inside a parallel tool call, a typecheck watch, a test runner, an undo snapshot or another background task of a turn ends only that task or that turn, with its stack in a crash file or the trace, instead of ending tofu."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc12-fix5","heading":"0.5.15-rc12-fix5 - 2026-10-21","body":"### Added\n\n- A lead that manages a board lists its tickets with `ticket_list`, by status, oldest first with the time since each last changed, up to ten and how many more; the board rule names it instead of a shell command.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- `tofu settings` and the `tofu drive` header print projectManagement as it is in force: on because the project has a board, or off until it has one, instead of off while the board rules were on.\n- A code block still streaming draws plain in the theme's text colour and highlights when its closing fence arrives, and the finished part of a reply is drawn once and appended: a frame inside a long code block takes about MS where it took 11."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc12-fix4","heading":"0.5.15-rc12-fix4 - 2026-10-21","body":"### Fixed\n\n- The lead's board check-in lists every ticket in review on its boards, oldest first with the time since each last changed, up to ten and how many more; before, it listed only tickets its own sub-agents held, so reviews from earlier sessions were never shown. It adds no step to an ordinary turn.\n- `tofu boardy lint` names a live ticket assigned to an agent type that does not exist, since a spawn for it is refused."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc12-fix3","heading":"0.5.15-rc12-fix3 - 2026-10-21","body":"### Fixed\n\n- A model you bind to the orchestrator in Models runs the next turn at once, and the footer shows it the moment you pick it; before, a model picked earlier with Ctrl+L, or kept by the session, outranked it and the turn ran on the old subscription. A role bound to any subscription or key chooses its own wire, and a sub-agent role applies whatever the lead runs on. A subscription is the default only when nothing is picked.\n- A switch to another vendor mid-conversation carries the history without the old vendor's thinking signatures, so the new vendor does not refuse it.\n- A refusal from a vendor reads as one sentence: which account, what the vendor said, and what to do next, such as setting up billing, signing in again or picking another model with Ctrl+L. The raw answer stays in the work card, and the every-account-limited note names the limit and its reset.\n\n### Changed\n\n- The board lead's rule asks it to review every ticket in review on its boards each turn, oldest first, close each from its Log, code and commit, and drop or merge tickets that are dead, duplicated or replaced."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc12-fix2","heading":"0.5.15-rc12-fix2 - 2026-10-18","body":"### Fixed\n\n- A sub-agent's edits stream `file.edit` again, so the desk's File edits tile and the terminal's edits pane show them; 0.5.15-rc12-fix1 dropped them. An appended write now streams `file.edit` with the appended lines as an added hunk, from the lead and from a sub-agent.\n- `tofu session NAME` on an 80-generation session answers in about 0.7 s where it took 2 s, with the same output: it reads each generation's event heads, four at a time, instead of parsing every event in full."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc12-fix1","heading":"0.5.15-rc12-fix1 - 2026-10-18","body":"### Fixed\n\n- Each tool result opens with its reference, `[TOOLREF1]`, so the lead can `recall` an earlier result by name; 0.5.15-rc12 said the lead could use its own call id, and on a real run it never did. A result costs N bytes more and keeps its bytes once sent, a repeated read points at the first read's reference, and an empty `recall` says what it needs."},{"version":"0.5.15-rc12","heading":"0.5.15-rc12 - 2026-10-18","body":"The lead knows what changed and what it already keeps.\n\n### Added\n\n- After an upgrade, the lead's first request in a session carries the changelog sections between the version its last turn ran on and this one, capped at 6 KiB, in the turn's first message so the cached prompt holds.
