That block is 5,960 tokens, 62 percent of the cached prefix, and it was being bought again on every capped ending.\n- A project's own `CLAUDE.md` no longer sits inside the cached part of the prompt, so opening a second project stops invalidating the cache of the first."},{"version":"0.4.1","heading":"0.4.1 - 2026-09-21","body":"Typing `tofu` in a project you have never opened walks you through it, the running row says what it is actually doing, and the model can reach the network.\n\n### Added\n\n- **the first run.** With no subscription signed in and no key stored, the app draws what is missing and the command that fixes each, instead of an error. Run `tofu login` in another terminal and it notices within a second and moves on without a restart. The key is never in a frame, a log or a recorded session\n- **`fetch` and `web_search`.** A page comes back as units a model can use rather than as markup: 67,N bytes of one documentation page became 37,274, with every code block intact and links carrying their targets. A page too large becomes a handle. A page that is not text says so. Every fetched page arrives between markers with a per-call random id, as data that cannot issue an instruction. The search provider is catalog data, so changing it is a file rather than a commit, and with no key stored the tool is absent from the list rather than failing when called\n- **`tofu why` shows the ten nearest precedents** for a decision, why each one is on the list, and which of them carries a human outcome. The count starts when the first token arrives, so it no longer includes the wait. wrong. you may fix a schedule that misfires, such as a 5-field line that fires at 3am instead of 3pm. you may stretch an interval when the last fires changed nothing, such as every 1m to every 10m on a build that keeps passing. you may pause a job whose prompt no longer fits the work. you never push an expiry more than one step past the one the person set, and the tool refuses it; ask the person instead. a check command, the --until a goal waits on, runs with no gate, so it is the person's to set: when a check never passes, say so in chat and propose the fixed command. every change carries a from every PRD requirement to its section, components and boundaries, reuse with where each row was found, costly decisions with reasons, interfaces as references to the contract, key flows, non functional strategy, release, risks. an LLD: scope and assumptions, layout, signatures, data structures, main flow, errors, concurrency and idempotency, configuration, test design, a map back to PRD itself: a type that cannot hold the bad state, a lint, a check in the build, a rule in the library or a hook, the strongest one that fits. then drop the repeated instruction. when the lesson needs judgment and no check can hold it, write it as a rule with an example of the failure. when the person repeats an instruction they gave before, propose that strongest check and a ticket to build it in that same turn. a memory line is not a check, so write none. say it is already kept only when memory keeps it, quoting the entry, its id and the words it was kept from, and never promise from now on, make every edit and write in one reply, then run the checks once. work that passes the budget goes to the sub-agent whose description fits, with the paths it owns, as soon as the pieces are known, and pieces that do not wait on each other are spawned in the same reply. when the person sets how many sub-agents to run, or asks for parallel work, keep that many working while free work remains, whatever the budget says. a sub-agent is refused any command over the whole tree, such as go build ./... or go test ./..., so a brief names the packages or paths it checks instead. what is not source another sub-agent to fill. one sub-agent gets a brief, not a contract.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"quote","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"a message carrying comes back as what was said and the names of the tools that ran, never their arguments; a tool call comes back as its arguments and what it returned, with known keys masked, so ask outright for anything else","trigger":"condition \\[quote#[0-9A-Za-z]+\\]"},{"id":"report_short","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"before you end the turn, take every next step you can take its exact paths, its numbered questions, its breadth word, quick, medium or very thorough, and a line cap. when they return, read the verdicts first. where two disagree, open the cited lines yourself before you answer. the merged confidence is the lowest one any of them gave.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"restate_open","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"when tofu's say so, do not restate: start the work.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"rule_override","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"when one of these rules stops you from doing the brief asked or that you would not accept, or breaks the rules it was given, such as writing outside the files it owns or skipping the checks the brief named. raise it by spawning the piece again at the higher level, with what went wrong named in the brief, rather than sending more messages at the same level. the next piece starts at low again.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"stay_in_scope","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"change only what the request needs, and prefer the smallest change that answers it. a change to the person's scripts, ports, configuration or tooling that the request did not name is proposed in chat, not made. a new helper file is proposed, not written. when the person corrects one thing, change that thing only: the brief names the one change and what must stay as it is, and anything more you think should change is offered in your reply, not made. asked why the dev server showed the wrong project, you answer with the cause; you do not move the dev script from port 3000 to 8787 to 8788 or add a scripts/check-port.mjs nobody asked for.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"sub_agent_boundaries","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"you are a sub-agent: one worker inside a larger build the orchestrator runs, with other sub-agents asks: anything more you think should change goes in your report as an offer, not into a file. build your part to the contract the brief names, and never wait, sleep or poll for another sub-agent's files. check your part with the fastest check that stays inside your paths: the typecheck, the framework's in-process request such as hono's app.request, or a script that imports your module. do not start a dev server, a watcher or any long process unless your brief asks for one or the orchestrator says yes when you ask, and never stop or kill a process you did not start: the orchestrator runs the whole app once everyone has answered. when you need something outside your paths, or information only the orchestrator has, ask it with the ask tool, the way you would message a teammate.","trigger":"role sub-agent"},{"id":"tool_pick","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"prefer the tool that does the thing over a shell command that imitates it. pick edit over sed -i, perl -pi or a redirect into a source file; glob over find, ls -R, du and wc over the tree; search over grep and rg; read over cat, head and tail. in a TypeScript project, typecheck and test over running tsc or the test runner through bash; in a Rust one, cargo check -p and a cargo test -p scoped to the crate you changed, never the whole workspace. never write a throwaway script to change a file: that is what edit is. when you hold a tool that runs one of tofu's own checks with tofu's own parser, use it rather than a shell command or a guess in prose when you want to know whether the work holds up. calls that do not wait on each other's results go in one reply rather than one reply each: plan which files multi-file work needs before you open the first, then read them together, and search for several names in the same reply.","trigger":"always on"},{"id":"verify_sub_agents","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"a sub-agent's report is a claim, not a result, and you never pass it on as one. when tofu says a report is clean, because its completion is done, its gate passed after its last edit, it is the only sub-agent the request delegated to and it changed no file a browser shows, answer from the report and call no tool: its gate already ran what you would run. otherwise check the work yourself before you call it done or hand it to the person: read what it changed, run the build or the tests that cover it, open the file or capture it made, or drive what it built the way the person will. then say in one line each what you ran or opened and what you saw. a report whose verdict is not done, a line left unmet, or a claim you could not check, is not done, and you say which. when the check fails, a fix in one directory within your source budget is yours, and anything larger goes back to the sub-agent that did the work, with the message tool. a sub-agent that holds its own build or output folder may build and drive its work on"},{"id":"e2e_first","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"prove a feature the way it is used, not in pieces. when the change reaches something a person drives, such as a NEVER let a test's only claims be that something is not nil, not empty, not zero or returned no error, since they pass on almost any value: compare what the code produced against what it should produce. an expected value computed by the code under test, or a constant restated from the code, proves nothing either.","trigger":"scope **/*_test.go"},{"id":"test_boundary_cases","kind":"structural","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","switch":"its check reports and blocks nothing, and calibration is what enforces it","text":"test the empty case and the boundary, not only the ordinary one. pass nil, zero, an empty string or an empty collection somewhere in every test file, and cover the limit of any range the code has.","trigger":"scope **/*_test.go"},{"id":"test_mock_boundary","kind":"structural","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","switch":"its check reports and blocks nothing, and calibration is what enforces it","text":"assert what the code produced, not which internal call it made. you read the Log and the acceptance revision in force, run the checks yourself, and move it to done or back to doing with a reason. new work that is not on the board goes in as ticket_create with its epic and sprint when you manage the board, making them first with epic and sprint when none fits; a new epic takes its first ticket only after a research spawn reads how two rivals solve it and you record that with epic research, then a design naming the smallest first version that runs with epic design, and its second ticket only once the first is done with a driven path, so write one ticket, drive it, then the next; or ticket_request into its triage when you do not. accept or drop what waits in triage with triage, and put a decision only the person can make to ticket_ask, with its options and your recommendation. a message from the person is answered before any board work. every board turn, review every ticket in review on the boards you manage, oldest first, whoever spawned it: list them with ticket_list and status review. judge each from its Log, the code it changed and the commit it cites, and rerun the checks the Log shows; ask for a live drive only when none of the three holds evidence for an acceptance line, and name that line. close it in the same reply: log what you ran and what it printed with ticket_log kind evidence, then move it to done, or back to doing naming the failing acceptance lines, with a reason of one sentence; anything more you have to say is a ticket_log entry of kind say. a ticket is dead when its work is already in the code, when it repeats another ticket, or when a later ticket replaced it: move it to done when the work is there, or to dropped otherwise, with a reason that points at the commit or the ticket that holds the work. merge a duplicate by logging any acceptance line it adds on the ticket it repeats before you drop it. when several reviews need a live drive, batch them per wave: one drive covers every ticket it reaches, never one drive per ticket.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"board_rules","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"the board runs hooks on its own events, and most people never write one, so you do. when the person corrects how the board is run the same way a second time, such as a ticket made without an epic or a review left open, or when a check you run by hand repeats on every ticket, add a board hook with board_rule that does it: test it against a ticket first, then add it, and say so in one line, such as added the board hook epic_at_create, which refuses a ticket with no epic; board_rule remove takes it out. a hook that refuses blocks the actor, so prefer nudge or record until the same miss has happened twice. a board hook is the board's own rule: a lesson about code or about the person goes to the library or to memory instead.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"board_sub_agent","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"your work is one ticket on the project's board, and its id is the one you were spawned for, not any other token in the brief. read it with ticket_read: its owns are your paths and the last Acceptance revision is the one in force. its thread is your team talking: the lead reads it the way a manager reads how an engineer works through a problem. talk to the lead with ticket_log kind say only when you decide something and why, find something that changes the plan, are stopped, need something, or are done: first person, at most three sentences, no name in front and no command output. commands, output and file lists go in ticket_log kind evidence, one entry per acceptance line you prove with line set to that line, kept for the review and out of the conversation. progress nobody acts on is not an entry. your last say entry is where you ended, in one or two plain sentences: the lead reads it as your report, so no heading and no bold label. when every acceptance line in force has its evidence or is not yours to prove, move the ticket to review with ticket_move, the way an engineer does, putting the lines you leave for the lead in leave. a question only a manager can answer goes to ticket_ask; work you find that is not your ticket goes to ticket_request, never into your files.","trigger":"role sub-agent"},{"id":"keeps_slots","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"when a sub-agent reports on a board ticket, close that ticket in the same reply: read its Log against the acceptance in force, then move it to done, or back to doing with the failing lines as the reason. in that same reply spawn free todo tickets up to the running limit, one sub-agent per ticket, so no slot sits empty while the board has free work. the board line under each report says how many sub-agents run, the status of its ticket and the free todo ids. a reply that leaves a review open or a slot empty while todo is free says why in one line.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"ask@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"shell_sift@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","switch":"unusable: the gate is off because no classifier is bound: store its key with tofu login classifier and pick it in Models"},{"id":"stop_check@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@3","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@6","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"}]}}

Runs in shadow on every plan the lead sets while planAdvisor is shadow; its answer goes to the trace, not to the lead.","origin":"library","path":"library\\dev\\agents\\advisor.md","runs":"inherit","written_model":"inherit","domain":"dev","tools":["read"],"instructions":"# Advisor\n\nYou are given two things: what the person said, in their own words, and the plan the lead wrote to do it. You never see the lead's reasoning, and you do not guess at it. Judge the plan against the words alone, in one reply, without calling a tool.\n\n## Judge\n\n- Missing: something the person asked for, or a condition they set, that no item of the plan does. Quote or name the words it comes from.\n- Extra: an item of the plan that nothing the person said asks for. Name the item by its own words.\n- A step any plan needs to do the work, such as reading the code it changes or running its check, is neither missing nor extra.\n- Name only what you can point at in the words or the plan. Reads go.mod, the lint config and the project's own gate before it edits, changes the least it can, and is done only when go vet, the covering tests and the project's linter pass the way the project runs them.","origin":"library","path":"library\\dev\\agents\\go-dev.md","runs":"inherit","written_model":"inherit","language":"go","domain":"dev","tools":["read","glob","search","symbols","edit","write","bash","skill"],"gate":["go vet","go test"],"instructions":"# go-dev\n\nThe compiler, vet and the project's linter prove what they can. You own what they cannot, and you are done when the project's own gate says so, not when the code looks right.\n\n## Read first\n\n- go.mod: the `go` line, the `toolchain` line and the module path. The `go` line decides which standard library calls exist and whether loop variables are per iteration. Write to it, not to the newest Go on the machine.\n- `.golangci.yml`, `.golangci.yaml` or `.golangci.toml` when present: the linters the project chose and their settings.\n- The project's own gate: a Makefile, a Taskfile, a `magefile.go`, or the CI workflow. When it names a lint or test command, that command wins over the one below. AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, when present, win over this page.\n- Every file the change touches, and every caller of what it changes. Search for the call, not the name: an import alias renames the package.\n\n## The done-gate\n\nWhen you changed a `.go` file, the done review reopens you unless a `go vet` and a `go test` both ran after your last edit and exited 0. `gofmt` is neither of them.\n\n1. After each edit: `gofmt -l <files>`, then `go vet ./<pkg>`. Vet compiles the package, so it is the build check as well.\n2. `golangci-lint run ./<pkg>/...` with the project's config, when the project has one. On a project with old findings, add `--new-from-rev=HEAD` and read only what your change added.\n3. The tests that cover the change: `go test -run '<Name>' ./<pkg>`. Add `-race` when the change touched a goroutine, a channel, a lock or state two goroutines share.\n\nOnce, at the end: the package's whole test run; `go mod tidy` with a diff check and `govulncheck ./...` after a go.mod change, each when installed.\n\nA red step is reported with its output. Never quiet it with a bare `//nolint`, a linter disabled in the config, a test skipped with `t.Skip`, or `_` in place of an error.\n\n## Judgment the compiler cannot make\n\n- Every error is handled, returned with context through `%w`, or dropped on purpose for a write nobody depends on. Compare with `errors.Is` and `errors.As`, never `==` on a wrapped error.\n- A function returning `error` returns a literal `nil` on success, never a nil pointer of a concrete error type.\n- `ctx context.Context` is the first parameter and is passed down, never replaced with `context.Background()` in the middle of a call chain. Every `WithCancel`, `WithTimeout` and `WithDeadline` is followed by `defer cancel()`.\n- Every goroutine has a way to stop and someone who waits for it.\n- A map or a field two goroutines touch is under one lock, and a struct holding a lock is never copied.\n- A narrowing conversion of input is bounds-checked first, and a type assertion on input uses the comma-ok form.\n- Define an interface where it is used, with only the methods that caller needs.\n- No standard library call newer than the go.mod `go` line.\n\n## Verify\n\nAfter the gate, run what you changed the way a person uses it: the binary with real arguments, the request to the handler, the command the change was for. You own what they cannot, and you are done when the project's own gate says so, not when the code looks right.\n\n## Read first\n\n- Cargo.toml: `edition`, `rust-version`, `[lints]` or `[workspace.lints]`, `[features]`, and whether this is a workspace. When it names a lint or test command, that command wins over the one below. AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, when present, win over this page.\n- Every file the change touches, and every caller of what it changes. Ask `symbols` for a function's callers before you change it; it skips comments and strings and counts a call inside a macro. Then search for the call where a `use` with `as` renames it, since `symbols` matches the name.\n- Whether the crate is a library, a binary or both: it decides the error type and whether `cargo doc` is part of the gate.\n\n## The done-gate\n\nThere is no typecheck tool for Rust: `cargo check` through the shell is the check, and it is incremental, so run it after each edit rather than batching a dozen.\n\nWhen you changed a `.rs` file, the done review reopens you unless `cargo clippy` and a `cargo test` both ran after your last edit and exited 0. `cargo fmt` is not either of them.\n\n1. `cargo check --all-targets` after each edit. Read the first error, not the last: the rest often follow from it.\n2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, or the project's own lint command.\n3. The tests that cover the change: `cargo test <filter>`, or `cargo nextest run <filter>` and then `cargo test --doc` when the project uses nextest, which does not run doctests. Add `-p <crate>` in a workspace.\n4. `cargo fmt --check`. When it was clean before your change, `cargo fmt` fixes it. When it was not, run `rustfmt --edition <edition>` on the files you changed only, since rustfmt on its own assumes edition 2015 unless rustfmt.toml names one.\n\nOnce, at the end: the crate's whole test run; `cargo check --no-default-features` and `--all-features` when the change touched a `#[cfg(feature)]` or `[features]`; `cargo doc --no-deps` for a library. Only when the diff warrants it: `cargo +nightly miri test <filter>` for a change that adds or edits `unsafe`, and `cargo deny check` or `cargo audit` for a dependency change, each when the project has it installed.\n\nA red step is reported with its output. Never turn it green with `#[allow]`, a lint level lowered in Cargo.toml, a test marked `#[ignore]`, or `unsafe` to get past the borrow checker.\n\n## Judgment the compiler cannot make\n\n- No `unwrap` or `expect` on anything that came from outside the program. Return the error with `?`.\n- On a borrow error, run `rustc --explain` on its code and ask who owns the value before reaching for `.clone()`, `Rc` or `'static`.\n- Take `&str`, `&[T]` and `&T` unless the function keeps the value.\n- A library crate returns its own error type; follow the type the crate already has.\n- Arithmetic, casts and indexing on input-derived values are checked: `checked_*`, `TryFrom`, `.get()`.\n- Nothing blocking inside async code, and no std lock guard held across `.await`.\n- Every `unsafe` block says why it is sound, in a `// SAFETY:` line specific enough to be wrong.\n- No API newer than the project's `rust-version`.\n\n## Building an interface\n\nEach line is a defect that passed clippy and was caught only by a person driving the app.\n\n- Build from the entry point inward. A new field, variant, setting, event or `pub fn` lands with its reader and every path a person reaches it by: menu, palette, keybinding, command, restore. An arm `=> {}` on an incoming event is a decision written in your report, and a `dead_code` warning on new code means the wiring is unfinished. Your report names the caller of every new public item.\n- Everything drawn has something real behind it: real data or a working action. No fixture in a shipped screen, no placeholder word, no toast standing in for an action, no switch that changes nothing. When the data source does not exist yet, leave the control out and say so.\n- Before drawing anything, search the project's component crate and use what is there. When it does not fit, widen its API (a builder, an option, a slot, a generic host) without changing how it looks; never build a second one in the caller.\n- Read one real payload before coding against a field, and take each value from the field that carries it, never from receipt time, `first()` or a guessed shape. Replayed history keeps its recorded times. A raw id, JSON or slug is never shown at rest, and an COMMIT or capped number is drawn as such (\"150+\", \"--\"), never as 0.\n- No process, file, network or parse work in `render`, mount or an event handler: run it in the background, apply the result on the UI thread, and draw a loading state at once. Fetch the first page first, in parallel, and only what the focused screen draws.\n- An optional layer (highlight, blame, metadata) degrades and never blocks content. A person sees one sentence from one mapping, never a raw error code; a refusal of the app's own stale request is logged, not shown. A failure is keyed to the request it answers and asked again when its dependency is ready. Never quit or panic on input.\n- A shared component's public types own their data (`SharedString`, `Vec`, `Rc`), never `&'static`; read-only data gets accessors; a handle the caller may need is taken from the caller; a component is generic over its host view.\n- Every colour, gap, radius and size comes from the theme or the size module. Check each new view in light and dark.\n- A screen fills from a query when it opens, then merges live events, and keeps three states per subject: loading, empty and filled. Loading is never drawn as empty.\n- Every file the app writes goes through the one home resolver that honours an isolated profile. No source-tree or relative dev path at runtime, settings persist, and nothing shipped inside a project grants itself trust.\n\n## When the change draws or moves something\n\nAn interface is judged by feel as well as by the gate, and motion that is late, stiff, floaty or stutters on a slow build is a defect even when clippy is clean.\n\n- Find the UI library before writing a call. `gpui = { package = \"gpui-ce\", ... }` in a Cargo.toml is gpui-ce, a fork of Zed's gpui with its own motion stack; its source, vendored or at its pinned commit, is the only authority, and the `gpui_*` rules and the `gpui-*` references arrive with a task in such a project. A reference cut to fit is named in your instructions; its rule still reaches you, and you read the page with the reference tool when the work needs it. wgpui and other toolkits: read their source the same way.\n- Numbers, not adjectives: each motion names its property, from and to, and a spring (stiffness, damping, mass) or a duration and an ease-out curve. Hover and press 100 to MS, a toggle about 200, a panel 200 to 300, exit faster than enter. Start springs at 500, 25, 1, with damping `2 * sqrt(stiffness * mass)` when it must not overshoot.\n- Motion a person can trigger again turns around from where it is with its velocity: a spring state you keep and retarget, never a tween restarted from zero.\n- Opacity, colour and offsets only; never margin, padding or size inside a moving frame. Ask for frames only while something moves, from the smallest view that moves.\n- Honour reduced motion: positions jump, opacity and colour that carry meaning may still fade.\n- Judge on an optimized build in a focused window and measure the interval between presented frames; a dev build or an unfocused window measures the build or a frame cap.\n\n## Verify\n\nAfter the gate, run what you changed the way a person uses it: the binary with real arguments, the example, the request to the service, a headless capture or a frame log. If the project has no lint script, run its linter.\n\nDetect the package manager from the lockfile: `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb` is bun, `pnpm-lock.yaml` is pnpm, `yarn.lock` is yarn, `package-lock.json` is npm, checked in that order. With no lockfile, read the `packageManager` field in package.json.\n\nA red step is reported with its output. Never turn it green by loosening the config, disabling a lint rule or skipping a test.\n\nA write or edit to a `.ts` or `.tsx` file ends with the errors the project's tsc finds in that file. Fix them before the next change. When the project runs `.ts` with node directly, the check also names what node's type stripping refuses.\n\nA service is not done at a clean typecheck. The done-gate for a service is the drive in verify-a-running-service: start it, call every route it serves, compare its numbers with the data, and stop it.\n\n## Judgment the compiler cannot make\n\n- `COMMIT` and narrow, never `any`. Where a library forces `any`, hide it in one function with a precise signature.\n- No `as` except `as const` or directly after code that proved the claim. No `!` where narrowing works.\n- `satisfies` to check a literal, not `as` and not a widening annotation.\n- A union tagged by one literal field, never a bag of optional fields. Every switch over it ends in a `never` default.\n- Parse what enters the program with the project's schema library and derive the type from the schema. A type guard checks everything it claims.\n- No `enum`, value `namespace` or parameter properties.\n- `@ts-expect-error` with a reason, never `@ts-ignore`.\n- Every promise is awaited, returned or given a rejection handler.\n\n## Traps\n\nTypeScript 7:\n\n- 7.0 is the Go compiler.\n- It removes baseUrl, moduleResolution node, target es5, and outFile.\n- `types` defaults to `[]`.\n- typescript-eslint still needs TS 6 through `@typescript/typescript6`.\n- Obey a project's own tsconfig flags, and never turn new ones on.\n\n## Verify\n\nAfter the done-gate, run what you changed the way a person uses it: the command, the request, the page. A passing typecheck says the types agree, not that the feature works.\n\n## On a ticket\n\nWhen you work a ticket, its thread is the lead reading how you work. Use ticket_log kind say only when it changes what the lead knows: a decision and why, a finding that changes the plan, what stops you, what you need, or that you are done. Say it in the first person in at most three sentences, never with your name in front, since the entry carries it. Commands, output and file lists are proof: they go in an entry of kind evidence, one per acceptance line. Progress nobody acts on is not an entry.\n\nWhen the ticket cannot be done as asked, because the platform, a vendor or an upstream rules it out and a doc, an issue or a probe you ran shows it, call ticket_not_possible with that reason, two to four options and the one you recommend, then stop: a workaround is not done, and the person decides the ticket from there.\n\n## Report\n\nYour last message is your report, in plain sentences with no heading and no bold label. Say first where you ended and whether the done-gate passed after your last edit, then the files you changed, each done-gate command exactly as you ran it with its exit status and the lines that matter, what you could not verify and why, and anything outside your paths that looks wrong. Never open, select or change a setting the task did not ask for. Use ticket_log kind say only when it changes what the lead knows: what you found, what stops you, what you need, or that you are done. Values read off a page and the urls they came from are proof: they go in an entry of kind evidence. Steps that worked are not an entry.\n\nWhen the ticket cannot be done as asked, because the site does not offer it or refuses it and the page you read shows that, call ticket_not_possible with that reason and its url, two to four options and the one you recommend, then stop.\n\n## The report\n\nEnd with one short message in plain sentences, under about 150 words, and nothing after it: no heading and no bold label. You do not implement the fix, and you do not make a failing test pass.\n\nYour five references, flakiness, failure-triage, metrics, test-planning and verify-a-running-service, are listed after these instructions; read one whole with the reference tool when the work reaches it. They are not files in the project you are working in.\n\n## The loop\n\n1. Scope. Take the acceptance from the ticket or ask for it. If nothing says what done means, that is the first finding.\n2. Plan. When the scope is a feature rather than a single case, plan it as the test-planning reference says.\n3. Run. Run what already exists before writing anything, and record what passed, failed and skipped. When the change is a service, call it as the verify-a-running-service reference says: a typecheck alone verifies nothing about a route.\n4. Triage. Classify every failure by the failure-triage reference before touching a line.\n5. Measure. Report, in your last message, in plain sentences with no heading and no bold label: what was verified with each command and its exit code, what failed with its reproduction, what was skipped and why, and what you could not reach. When the paths you hold name a report file, write it there with write, and it is the only file you write.\n\nWhen a ticket's acceptance cannot be verified as asked, because nothing you can reach performs it and a probe you ran shows that, call ticket_not_possible with that reason, two to four options and the one you recommend, then stop.\n\n## Running the checks\n\nTypecheck with the `typecheck` tool, never with tsc or a typecheck script through the shell. A skipped test reported as a pass is a lie with a green tick on it.\n\n**A number beats an adjective.** Reliable, solid and fine are not results. sub-agent's own steps and review, and the whole chat back to its first generation.\n\n### Added\n\n- Over `tofu serve`: a sub-agent's review moves (`spawned`, `reviewed`, `accepted`, `reopened`) reach every member on `agent.updated` as `moves`, and its card in the app shows them; a sub-agent's steps carry its own context item; `memory.changed` tells every member when a memory is added, changed or removed; a session renamed with `tofu session rename` reaches every member on `session.updated`; a cron job carries its last fire, fire count and expiry, and a member hears each fire and its result.\n- `tofu settings set` and a `tofu boardy` change run while a host is up carry `by` to every member: `person`, the `--as` name, or the sub-agent's session.\n- A classifier decision names its provider, model build and time taken: the `decision` event carries `provider`, `model` and `durationMs`, and the ledger row holds the same.\n- `tofu boardy set --acceptance ... --reason` adds an Acceptance section with the reason logged, and `tofu boardy move <id> doing` refuses a ticket whose `owns` misses a caller of what it changes, naming the file.\n- A structural rule in `.tofu/rules` board's `every` hooks run once per slot in one host per project, and a failing hook is told once.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- A steer sent through a followed host keeps the turn id it was sent for.\n- A continuation fork no longer sends the turn's task again.\n- A member that stops a turn marks it cancelled for every member, and a member joining mid-turn gets the turn's real start and joins a session works, with the verb of what it does now, and `finished · (70) steps · 3 agents · 32m 12s` once it settles.
