They are different quantities and the bar now shows the one a person watching a turn can act on.\n- **A file path read back out of the ledger, and a session handle typed on the command line, were both followed without a guard.** A path that leaves its root is refused, and the refusal cannot be mistaken for a missing file.\n- **A truncated tool result said only that something was missing.** It now says how many bytes were dropped, and when the whole output could not be stored it says that too, rather than leaving a hole with no explanation.\n\n### Changed\n\n- **A rule declares which of ten concerns it is, and the declaration is required.** Five concerns may never be conditional, so a rule that is about output shape, safety, the environment, tool guidance or the report format is refused if it declares a trigger at all. Two shipped rules were firing on the wrong trigger and one of them fired on a task naming only `CHANGELOG.md`.\n- **A rule fires on the language of the paths, the directories touched, or the verb the task names**, rather than on a path glob standing in for all three.\n- **The harness reports a median and a range over repeats rather than a mean.** A comparison where either arm has fewer than two passing repeats prints `not separable`, and a task that passes a gate on one repeat and fails on another is named unstable and ranks no arm.\n\n### Note\n\n**Three measurements in this release returned no, and that is the point of having them.** A moved cache breakpoint caches exactly as much as the old one, because the vendor looks back twenty content blocks and a turn here adds at most eight. The recorded corpus cannot separate a thrift arm from a shaping arm: six of 109 sessions carry both, and 22 sessions are one fixture written to produce reading. And the account picker cannot be scored against any arm yet, because until this release nothing ever wrote a quota reading down.\n\n**None of the 25 reports under `bench/` is built by rerunning its own code.** Every one is built from the text of its own markdown, and every one now says so on its page.\n\n**A recorded session written before this release keeps the old meaning of its occupancy** under the same key, and nothing in a row tells the two apart. Sessions recorded before event ids existed get a derived id when quoted, which resolves the same way every time but is not the id the record carried."},{"version":"0.4.8","heading":"0.4.8 - 2026-09-22","body":"`catalog` is `library`.\n\n### Changed\n\n- **The `catalog` directory is now `library`, and `tofu catalog` is now `tofu library`.** Two other tools already call the same thing a catalog, and a shared word made this look like a copy of theirs when the contents are ours. `library` also says the right thing: a place things are looked up from, rather than a list of what exists.\n- `tofu rules list` and `tofu rules check` take `--library` where they took `--catalog`.\n\n### Deprecated\n\n- **`tofu catalog` still runs and tells you the new name.** It goes at the next minor bump.\n\n### Note\n\nA decision recorded before today names its rule file by a `catalog/` path in the sentence `tofu why` prints. **Nothing resolves a path from that sentence**, so old decisions replay unchanged; the only effect is that `tofu why` on a row from before this release names a directory that no longer exists."},{"version":"0.4.7","heading":"0.4.7 - 2026-09-22","body":"More than one account, and a screen that stops lying about which one.\n\n### Added\n\n- **`tofu login --status` is a listing rather than a line.** Each subscription is a heading, each account under it carries the email it belongs to, the plan when the vendor reports one, and how full each quota window is. `--redact` masks the account when you are sharing a screen.\n- **A second account for the same subscription is stored and reachable.** Signing in again no longer overwrites the first one. When two are usable and nothing says which, tofu refuses and names both by number rather than picking by accident, and the listing says so with the command that sets one aside.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **A second Codex login used to overwrite the first.** A Codex credential stored without naming its account, so both rows collided. A login names its account now, and the row already on disk is repaired the first time tofu opens the store.\n- **With two accounts on one subscription, quota was polled for neither.** Each account is polled for its own windows, and a window is remembered against the account it belongs to rather than against the vendor.\n- **`tofu usage` said no credential was stored while listing two of them**, whenever every window was spent.\n- **The account was printed in full in the settings pane and masked in the listing.** One rule now, and the mask tells two accounts apart instead of rendering them identically.\n- **A command that succeeds and prints nothing is no longer sent as an empty message**, which some vendors refuse. An empty success and an empty failure also read differently now, so the model can tell a command that worked from one that broke.\n- **A turn that stops itself keeps its last word.** Tool calls left unanswered when the loop guard tripped made the final request malformed, so the explanation of why the turn stopped was the thing that got lost.\n\n### Changed\n\n- The token benchmark replays against a fixed commit instead of the working tree, so its numbers measure the cap rather than yesterday's edits."},{"version":"0.4.6","heading":"0.4.6 - 2026-09-21","body":"A rule file with one bad number no longer turns the gate off, a failed request is tried again, and the mouse works.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **A tool gate rule that cannot be satisfied now refuses to start a turn instead of running every call unjudged.** A missing key and an unusable rule were one branch, and both left the gate off behind the same banner. They are two now and they read differently on screen. **There was also no range check at all**, so a threshold of 1.85 on a zero to one scale loaded cleanly and asked the model anyway.\n- **Both subscription wires retry.** One overloaded answer used to end a turn five steps in. The retry window is the connection, never the stream, so a retried request can never repeat text already on your screen. **A step can now put five requests on the wire, and a retried one may still bill.**\n- **A one letter answer no longer approves a gate ask.** The answers are `1`, `2` and `3`. Typing a sentence that began with `a` under an open ask used to allow the call on its first character.\n- A pale column down the left of the composer. It was a border glyph painted over the tint, and the tint is meant to be the only edge.\n- An id typed from the transcript reaches the work view. It was matched against the start of an id where the screen draws the end.\n\n### Added\n\n- **The mouse.** The five tabs and any trace id are clickable. Everything else on the screen still selects with a drag, and a drag that starts on a tab selects instead of switching.\n- **A gate ask says what tripped it in words**, using the wording the judge itself was given rather than a scale invented here. A decision recorded before this still prints its numbers.\n- **A command proxy, off by default**, set in `catalog/tools/shell/proxy.yaml`. It rewrites a shell command before the gate sees it, so the ledger records the command that actually ran. A project's own filter file is refused, and a proxy that crashes falls back to the raw command.\n- **`README.md`.** The repository now says what tofu is in its first line, that it is personal and not released, which judgments lost to their free arm and are switched off with the numbers that say so, how to build and drive the binary from a fresh checkout, and where in `bench/` the numbers live. There is still no `LICENSE`, so the default is all rights reserved.\n\n### Measured\n\n- A pasted screenshot costs about 1,765 tokens. 190,N bytes at 1536 by 850, measured against the same turn without it and cross-checked against the vendor's own area rule. **File size says almost nothing about the cost.**\n- A recorded session runs a median of 7 tool calls and at most 55. 1.5 percent of tool result bytes come off losslessly, and `glob` is 92 percent of the corpus by size with none removable.\n- Fifty three production failures published by another harness were checked against this tree: five were real and are named in `.local/boji/planning/doing/known-failures.md`.\n\n### Removed\n\n- **The `grep` tool is gone. `search` is the only way to find text.** Over a tree of 13,140 files the two tools took 48.5 s and 37 s for the same query, and returned SIZE against SIZE. **The removal is about the bytes, not the seconds:** a tool that hands back SIZE spends a context window on one call. `grep` could not be capped, because every cap tried cost half the correct answers on a thirty question bench, so it goes rather than shrinks. `search` now says in its own description that it finds text and that there is no grep tool, so a model does not reach for what is not there.\n\n### Changed\n\n- **`tofu search` reports what it scanned.** A call says how many files it looked at and how many it returned, and stops after 1,200 candidates rather than reading a whole tree. The cap has never fired on a real question."},{"version":"0.4.5","heading":"0.4.5 - 2026-09-21","body":"What is happening right now has its own line, and five things on screen have their own colour.\n\n### Added\n\n- **A progress line under the running summary.** The summary carries the counters and the line beneath it carries the one call happening now, with a spinner while it runs. It replaces itself, so a turn with twelve tool calls is still two lines. **The sub-agents view draws the same line for a child.**\n- Five things that were all the same dim now read as themselves: a tool call, a shell command, a file path, an event id, and a finished call.\n- Whether the running line counts shell calls separately is a setting.\n\n### Changed\n\n- **The separator above the composer is gone.** The tint already says where the input begins and two marks for one boundary is one too many.\n- **The composer has a blank row above and below its text, inside the tint**, so it reads as an area rather than a strip with words in it.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **A pasted image deleted from the message was still attached.** Two separate paths carried it: the chip list under the composer, and a list of files on disk that never looked at the message at all. **Both now keep only what the message still refers to.**"},{"version":"0.4.4","heading":"0.4.4 - 2026-09-21","body":"He ran it and wrote down what it drew.\n\n### Added\n\n- **`tofu frame` renders the interface to standard output and exits**, at any width and height, with `--plain` to strip the colour. The interface can now be read without being run, which is how three of the fixes below were found.\n- A progress line is not here yet. What is: the running line now reads `· (12) tools · jev 6 · shell (1) · 44s · [#c11]` and never names a tool.\n\n### Changed\n\n- **The clock starts when you press enter and stops when you have the final answer.** It no longer restarts on a phase, a request or a tool call, and only the word beside it changes. `requesting` appears once, before the first response of a message, and never again in that turn.\n- **A short id is the last six characters of the real one, not the first.** Every session id begins `turn-` and a hex timestamp, so for months every id on screen was the same six characters: `#turn-1` under everything.\n- **The running line counts tools rather than naming them.** A shell keeps its own count, because a process that outlives its call is a different kind of thing.\n- Headings render as headings. A second level heading printed its own hash marks, and every markdown fixture was a short handwritten string, so nothing caught it. The fixture is now a real recorded answer of 583 words.\n- Brackets mean a thing can be activated, `[1] chat` and `[#c11]`, and the whole label is the target, not the bracket.\n- A finished turn reads `cooked for 44s`.\n- **The arrow keys belong to the input and never move the transcript.** The wheel, `pgup` and `pgdown` scroll. On a hand labelled set of 57 paragraphs the default agrees 89 percent of the time, Jev 84 to 86 at a third of a cent and a second per message, and the brevity arm 26\n- `boji login openrouter` asks for the key without echoing it, proves it reaches Jev with one call, and only then writes it to `~/.boji/.env` at mode 600 where the platform honours it. A key that does not answer leaves nothing behind. The key is never an argument and never reaches a log. A project `.env` still wins over the stored one\n- `boji run` has six tools instead of three: `glob`, `grep` and `edit` join `read`, `write` and `bash`. `edit` takes an exact span of text and replaces it\n- `boji run` can call Boji. `boji lint comments`, `boji rules check` and `boji judge` are tools a turn may use, so an agent runs this project's own checks instead of imitating them. Recursion is bounded at depth 2\n- a child that reports done gets asked whether it is. `boji run --done-review typed` puts the claim through the `stop_check@1` battery and re-opens the child once, in words, with the reason and the decision id, so `boji why <id>` prints the chain behind the re-open. `--done-review cheap` is the arm that decides on whether any tool call ran clean, and `off` is the default and the behaviour until now. A Jev error leaves the claim standing with the reason on the child's row rather than re-opening on a broken backend\n- a spawn onto a path another child already holds returns that child, the glob that collided and what it has reported, instead of an error. The roster still refuses; the refusal now carries the one correct move\n- a turn can hand work to a child that owns its own paths, refused at the write if it strays, and refused outright if two children overlap. The child's row reaches the ledger as a turn of its own and the parent's cost covers the tree it started. `--no-crew` is the off arm\n- a context budget, with the byte-per-token figure measured on this project's own content rather than assumed\n- a session that outgrows its budget forks instead of being rewritten in place. The old session ends whole and a new one begins carrying the work forward, so the next request is one fresh prefix and then appends. Rewriting the middle of a live conversation costs 58 percent more than doing nothing at all, because it destroys the cache it was meant to save. The fork carries handles to what it dropped, which is instant; a written summary was measured at 21,MS, stale before it arrives, and saves 5 percent. The off arm is in the loop configuration and has no flag yet, unlike `--no-gate` and `--no-crew`\n- `boji run` asks the tool gate battery before every tool call and records the answer. The decision row names the turn and the turn row names the decision, so either one leads to the other\n- `boji run --no-gate` is the arm that turns the gate off, and `--max-decisions` caps the spend. A turn that reaches the cap ends with its own outcome rather than continuing quietly\n- `boji rules list` and `boji rules check [path]` run the rules in the catalog over a tree and print every fire with its mode, whether it blocked, and the override rate. `--catalog <dir>` points at a scratch catalog, so an enforced mode can be tried without touching the one that ships\n- a rule may declare an exception in its own file. `em_dash` declares `except: quoted`, so an em dash inside a fence, an indented block, a backtick span or a double-quoted span is the author quoting rather than the author writing\n- a turn session file carries a schema version, and a decision row carries the turn it came from\n\n### Changed\n\n- the shell tool runs `sh -c`, not `cmd /C`. On Windows `cmd` has no way to escape a quote inside a quoted argument, so 24 of 32 recorded quoted commands reached the tool as a literal backslash-quote, matched nothing, and returned empty with exit 1, which a model reads as an answer\n- the request to a subscription marks the conversation as cacheable, not only the system prompt and the tool list, and the cache lives an hour instead of five minutes. The token count is unchanged; what those tokens cost is not\n- the Codex request carries a cache key for the whole session, so its own prefix cache can find the previous step\n- `boji doctor` finds a key stored in the home file, from any directory, and still names where it looked when there is none\n- `boji run` sets a system prompt naming the tools it has. A tool a model is not told about is not offered, which is why the first run with six tools called neither `glob` nor `grep`\n- `boji rules list` and `boji rules check` carry their catalog in the binary, so they work in any tree rather than only in this repository. A project with its own `catalog/rules` still wins, and both verbs name which set decided, as a first line in text and as an `origin` field in `--json`\n- **breaking:** `boji rules list --json` emits `{\"origin\": ..., \"rules\": [...]}` where it emitted a bare array. A reader that expects an array at the top level needs one field of indirection\n- `boji_judge` takes a `state` and a `battery` instead of a raw json body. A model could not guess the old shape: in one recorded run it tried six times, first with a list, then with four different spellings of a question type, and failed every time\n- the stop check corpus is nineteen frozen files under `bench/stopcheck/`, not whatever the live ledger happens to hold. Running a turn in this repository no longer changes what a measurement is measured against\n- the three copies of the percentile arithmetic under `bench/` are one package, `bench/stat`. The three were identical, so no published figure moved\n- the boji arm of `bench harness` no longer measures whichever binary invoked it. It builds `./cmd/boji` and measures that, or measures the one named by `--boji <path>`\n\n### Removed\n\n- `boji bench` is gone, with its five targets. The measurement lives in its own binary, built from `bench/cmd`, so an edit under `bench/` cannot break `boji login`, `boji why` or any other verb. Run `go run ./bench/cmd <target>` from the repository root, or build it once with `go build -o bench ./bench/cmd`. `boji bench api` becomes `bench api`, and `cost`, `wording`, `turn` and `harness` follow the same way. Every flag is unchanged and the reports are byte for byte what they were\n\n### Fixed\n\n- the gate was off in every directory except this repository. The policy was looked for beside the project rather than inside the binary, and the key was read from `./.env` alone. The policy ships in the binary now, a project may override it, and the row says which one decided\n- the Codex wire made up a new session identity for every request, so nothing it sent could match anything it had sent before\n- a turn session file never recorded its schema version, so every one written before today reads as schema 0 against version 1\n- `boji judge` never recorded which state builder made its state, so `boji why` said the writer had not adopted it. Every row from `boji check` had it and no row from `boji judge` did"},{"version":"0.2.0","heading":"0.2.0 - 2026-09-18","body":"The record. Every decision can be explained and re-scored without asking the model again.\n\n### Added\n\n- `boji why <id>` prints the chain behind a decision: every answer with its distribution, the verdict, the rule that fired, the threshold it compared against, and a line naming any question that sat inside the dead band\n- `boji replay --point <name> --set <threshold>=<value>` re-scores every recorded decision against changed thresholds, with no network call in its import graph, and counts how many changed verdicts now disagree with a recorded outcome\n- `boji check '<command>'` decides on a real shell command and records the row without blocking anything, and `boji label <id> <outcome>` attaches the answer a person would have given\n- `boji lint comments` reports every comment in the tree with its position, using the standard library parser rather than a text match\n- a policy: thresholds as catalog data, a closed verdict type, authority nouls that relax and never tighten, and a dead band taken from the measured rerun spread\n- a state builder with a version derived from its own shape, recorded on the row\n\n### Changed\n\n- a ledger answer keeps the kind it was: a noul is a number, not a probability parsed out of a field named for a different answer kind. Schema 2, and rows written under schema 1 still read\n- the request cap is two documented token limits instead of one invented byte number, with an estimator built from five measured points and deliberately pessimistic where it has no data\n- a bare catalog name is refused when more than one version exists, naming every version it found, rather than silently taking the newest\n\n### Fixed\n\n- `boji check` put the command itself into the recent user messages, so a question about what the user asked for answered 0.91 about a request nobody made, relaxing a force-push from ask to allow. It is 0.03 and ask now\n- `boji doctor` reported the key as missing while `boji judge` was using it, and now names where the key came from\n- a converter existed three times and two copies silently dropped a choice option's criteria"},{"version":"0.1.0","heading":"0.1.0 - 2026-09-18","body":"The instrument. A typed decision can be asked, validated, recorded and measured.\n\n### Added\n\n- `boji judge` reads a state and a question battery on standard input and prints typed answers, writing a row for every call and answering a repeat from cache with no network\n- `boji bench api` measures latency by state size and question count, rerun agreement, the option ceiling and cost per decision, and writes a dated report\n- `boji bench cost` compares Jev, two frontier models and a plain regular expression on the same six decisions\n- `boji doctor`, `boji catalog resolve`, `boji version`\n- the Jev wire with structural validation: probabilities that sum, a chosen option inside its criteria, an argmax that agrees, a score level count that matches\n- the decision ledger, append only, one file per day, with the full distribution on every answer, and a replay cache keyed on canonical JSON\n- the question catalog with a build-time linter, and a YAML subset parser written by hand rather than taking a dependency"}]}}

the brief asked or that you would not accept, or breaks the rules it was given, such as writing outside the files it owns or skipping the checks the brief named. raise it by spawning the piece again at the higher level, with what went wrong named in the brief, rather than sending more messages at the same level. the next piece starts at low again.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"stay_in_scope","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"change only what the request needs, and prefer the smallest change that answers it. a change to the person's scripts, ports, configuration or tooling that the request did not name is proposed in chat, not made. a new helper file is proposed, not written. when the person corrects one thing, change that thing only: the brief names the one change and what must stay as it is, and anything more you think should change is offered in your reply, not made. asked why the dev server showed the wrong project, you answer with the cause; you do not move the dev script from port 3000 to 8787 to 8788 or add a scripts/check-port.mjs nobody asked for.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"sub_agent_boundaries","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"you are a sub-agent: one worker inside a larger build the orchestrator runs, with other sub-agents building the other parts at the same time. your brief is your whole job and the paths you hold are your whole reach. open every reference your brief names before you start, and change only what it asks: anything more you think should change goes in your report as an offer, not into a file. build your part to the contract the brief names, and never wait, sleep or poll for another sub-agent's files. check your part with the fastest check that stays inside your paths: the typecheck, the framework's in-process request such as hono's app.request, or a script that imports your module. do not start a dev server, a watcher or any long process unless your brief asks for one or the orchestrator says yes when you ask, and never stop or kill a process you did not start: the orchestrator runs the whole app once everyone has answered. when you need something outside your paths, or information only the orchestrator has, ask it with the ask tool, the way you would message a teammate.","trigger":"role sub-agent"},{"id":"tool_pick","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"prefer the tool that does the thing over a shell command that imitates it. pick edit over sed -i, perl -pi or a redirect into a source file; glob over find, ls -R, du and wc over the tree; search over grep and rg; read over cat, head and tail. in a TypeScript project, typecheck and test over running tsc or the test runner through bash; in a Rust one, cargo check -p and a cargo test -p scoped to the crate you changed, never the whole workspace. never write a throwaway script to change a file: that is what edit is. when you hold a tool that runs one of tofu's own checks with tofu's own parser, use it rather than a shell command or a guess in prose when you want to know whether the work holds up. calls that do not wait on each other's results go in one reply rather than one reply each: plan which files multi-file work needs before you open the first, then read them person: read what it changed, run the build or the tests that cover it, open the file or capture it made, or drive what it built the way the person will. then say in one line each what you ran or you read the Log and the acceptance revision in force, run the checks yourself, and move it to done or back to doing with a reason. new work that is not on the board goes in as ticket_create with its epic and sprint when you manage the board, making them first with epic and sprint when none fits; or ticket_request into its triage when you do not. accept or drop what waits in triage with triage, and put a decision only the person can make to ticket_ask, with its options and your recommendation. a message from the person is answered before any board work. every board turn, review every ticket in review on the boards you manage, oldest first, whoever spawned it: list them with ticket_list and status review. judge each from its Log, the code it changed and the commit it cites, and rerun the checks the Log shows; ask for a live drive only when none of the three holds evidence for an acceptance line, and name that line. close it in the same reply: log what you ran and what it printed with ticket_log kind evidence, then move it to done, or back to doing naming the failing acceptance lines, with a reason of one sentence; anything more you have to say is a ticket_log entry of kind say. a ticket is dead when its work is already in the code, when it repeats another ticket, or when a later ticket replaced it: move it to done when the work is there, or to dropped otherwise, with a reason that points at the commit or the ticket that holds the work. merge a duplicate by logging any acceptance line it adds on the ticket it repeats before you drop it. when several reviews need a live drive, batch them per wave: one drive covers every ticket it reaches, never one drive per ticket.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"board_rules","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"the board runs hooks on its own events, and most people never write one, so you do. when the person corrects how the board is run the same way a second time, such as a ticket made without an epic or a review left open, or when a check you run by hand repeats on every ticket, add a board hook with board_rule that does it: test it against a ticket first, then add it, and say so in one line, such as added the board hook epic_at_create, which refuses a ticket with no epic; board_rule remove takes it out. a hook that refuses blocks the actor, so prefer nudge or record until the same miss has happened twice. a board hook is the board's own rule: a lesson about code or about the person goes to the library or to memory instead.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"board_sub_agent","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"your work is one ticket on the project's board, and its id is the one you were spawned for, not any other token in the brief. read it with ticket_read: its owns are your paths and the last Acceptance revision is the one in force. its thread is your team talking: the lead reads it the way a manager reads how an engineer works through a problem. talk to the lead with ticket_log kind say only when you decide something and why, find something that changes the plan, are stopped, need something, or are done: first person, at most three sentences, no name in front and no command output. commands, output and file lists go in ticket_log kind evidence, one entry per acceptance line you prove with line set to that line, kept for the review and out of the conversation. progress nobody acts on is not an entry. your last say entry is where you ended, in one or two plain sentences: the lead reads it as your report, so no heading and no bold label. when every acceptance line in force has its evidence or is not yours to prove, move the ticket to review with ticket_move, the way an engineer does, putting the lines you leave for the lead in leave. a question only a manager can answer goes to ticket_ask; work you find that is not your ticket goes to ticket_request, never into your files.","trigger":"role sub-agent"},{"id":"keeps_slots","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"off","switch":"off until the project has a board: tofu boardy init","text":"when a sub-agent reports on a board ticket, close that ticket in the same reply: read its Log against the acceptance in force, then move it to done, or back to doing with the failing lines as the reason. in that same reply spawn free todo tickets up to the running limit, one sub-agent per ticket, so no slot sits empty while the board has free work. the board line under each report says how many sub-agents run, the status of its ticket and the free todo ids. a reply that leaves a review open or a slot empty while todo is free says why in one line.","trigger":"role orchestrator"},{"id":"ask@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"shell_sift@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","switch":"unusable: the gate is off because no classifier is bound: store its key with tofu login classifier and pick it in Models"},{"id":"stop_check@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@1","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@3","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"},{"id":"tool_gate@6","kind":"point","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow"}]}}

a build that keeps passing. you may pause a job whose prompt no longer fits the work. you never push an expiry more than one step past the one the person set, and the tool refuses it; ask the person instead. a check command, the --until a goal waits on, runs with no gate, so it is the person's to set: when a check never passes, say so in chat and propose the fixed command. every change carries a from every PRD requirement to its section, components and boundaries, reuse with where each row was found, costly decisions with reasons, interfaces as references to the contract, key flows, non functional strategy, release, risks. an LLD: scope and assumptions, layout, signatures, data structures, main flow, errors, concurrency and idempotency, configuration, test design, a map back to PRD and HLD, open questions, and each add-on present or left out with a reason. this list is the template: do not search the project for a template file.","trigger":"condition (?i)\\b(prd|hld|lld|high[- on"},{"id":"spawn_effort","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"start each sub-agent at low effort, and settle every open choice in the brief yourself: the exact behaviour, the the brief asked or that you would not accept, or breaks the rules it was given, such as writing outside the files it owns or skipping the checks the brief named. raise it by spawning the piece again orchestrator"},{"id":"stay_in_scope","kind":"human","origin":"shipped","mode":"shadow","text":"change only what the request needs, and prefer the smallest change that answers it. a change to the Return the error with `?`.\n- On a borrow error, run `rustc --explain` on its code and ask who owns the value before reaching for `.clone()`, `Rc` or `'static`.\n- Take `&str`, `&[T]` and `&T` unless the function keeps the value.\n- A library crate returns its own error type; follow the type the crate already has.\n- Arithmetic, casts and indexing on input-derived values are checked: `checked_*`, `TryFrom`, `.get()`.\n- Nothing blocking inside async code, and no std lock guard held across `.await`.\n- Every `unsafe` block says why it is sound, in a `// SAFETY:` line specific enough to be wrong.\n- No API newer than the project's `rust-version`.\n\n## Building an interface\n\nEach line is a defect that passed clippy and was caught only by a person driving the app.\n\n- Build from the entry point inward. A new field, variant, setting, event or `pub fn` lands with its reader and every path a person reaches it by: menu, palette, keybinding, command, restore. An arm `=> {}` on an incoming event is a decision written in your report, and a `dead_code` warning on new code means the wiring is unfinished. Your report names the caller of every new public item.\n- Everything drawn has something real behind it: real data or a working action. No fixture in a shipped screen, no placeholder word, no toast standing in for an action, no switch that changes nothing. When the data source does not exist yet, leave the control out and say so.\n- Before drawing anything, search the project's component crate and use what is there. When it does not fit, widen its API (a builder, an option, a slot, a generic host) without changing how it looks; never build a second one in the caller.\n- Read one real payload before coding against a field, and take each value from the field that carries it, never from receipt time, `first()` or a guessed shape. Replayed history keeps its recorded times. A raw id, JSON or slug is never shown at rest, and an COMMIT or capped number is drawn as such (\"150+\", \"--\"), never as 0.\n- No process, file, network or parse work in `render`, mount or an event handler: run it in the background, apply the result on the UI thread, and draw a loading state at once. Fetch the first page first, in parallel, and only what the focused screen draws.\n- An optional layer (highlight, blame, metadata) degrades and never blocks content. A person sees one sentence from one mapping, never a raw error code; a refusal of the app's own stale request is logged, not shown. A failure is keyed to the request it answers and asked again when its dependency is ready. Never quit or panic on input.\n- A shared component's public types own their data (`SharedString`, `Vec`, `Rc`), never `&'static`; read-only data gets accessors; a handle the caller may need is taken from the caller; a component is generic over its host view.\n- Every colour, gap, radius and size comes from the theme or the size module. Check each new view in light and dark.\n- A screen fills from a query when it opens, then merges live events, and keeps three states per subject: loading, empty and filled. Loading is never drawn as empty.\n- Every file the app writes goes through the one home resolver that honours an isolated profile. No source-tree or relative dev path at runtime, settings persist, and nothing shipped inside a project grants itself trust.\n\n## When the change draws or moves something\n\nAn interface is judged by feel as well as by the gate, and motion that is late, stiff, floaty or stutters on a slow build is a defect even when clippy is clean.\n\n- Find the UI library before writing a call. `gpui = { package = \"gpui-ce\", ... }` in a Cargo.toml is gpui-ce, a fork of Zed's gpui with its own motion stack; its source, vendored or at its pinned commit, is the only authority, and the `gpui_*` rules and the `gpui-*` references arrive with a task in such a project. A reference cut to fit is named in your instructions; its rule still reaches you, and you read the page with the reference tool when the work needs it. wgpui and other toolkits: read their source the same way.\n- Numbers, not adjectives: each motion names its property, from and to, and a spring (stiffness, damping, mass) or a duration and an ease-out curve. Hover and press 100 to MS, a toggle about 200, a panel 200 to 300, exit faster than enter. Start springs at 500, 25, 1, with damping `2 * sqrt(stiffness * mass)` when it must not overshoot.\n- Motion a person can trigger again turns around from where it is with its velocity: a spring state you keep and retarget, never a tween restarted from zero.\n- Opacity, colour and offsets only; never margin, padding or size inside a moving frame. Ask for frames only while something moves, from the smallest view that moves.\n- Honour reduced motion: positions jump, opacity and colour that carry meaning may still fade.\n- Judge on an optimized build in a focused window and measure the interval between presented frames; a dev build or an unfocused window measures the build or a frame cap.\n\n## Verify\n\nAfter the gate, run what you changed the way a person uses it: the binary with real arguments, the example, the request to the service, a headless capture or a frame log. Run what you built inside your owns and your scratch folder, and put the command a person would type in your report, word for word, with what it printed. A clean clippy says the code is idiomatic, not that the feature works.\n\n## On a ticket\n\nWhen you work a ticket, its thread is the lead reading how you work. Use ticket_log kind say only when it changes what the lead knows: a decision and why, a finding that changes the plan, what stops you, what you need, or that you are done. Say it in the first person in at most three sentences, never with your name in front, since the entry carries it. Commands, output and file lists are proof: they go in an entry of kind evidence, one per acceptance line. Progress nobody acts on is not an entry.\n\nWhen the ticket cannot be done as asked, because the platform, a vendor or an upstream rules it out and a doc, an issue or a probe you ran shows it, call ticket_not_possible with that reason, two to four options and the one you recommend, then stop: a workaround is not done, and the person decides the ticket from there.\n\n## Report\n\nYour last message is your report, in plain sentences with no heading and no bold label. Say first where you ended and whether the gate passed after your last edit, then the files you changed, each gate command exactly as you ran it with its exit status and the lines that matter, any step you skipped and why, and anything outside your paths that looks wrong. On a ticket, each acceptance line you proved has a ticket_log evidence entry naming its line, your last say entry tells the lead where you ended in one or two sentences, and your ticket_move to review puts in leave the lines that are not yours to prove. A recipe's urls, a url you build and any other shortcut apply only after that path is done: then navigate to the recipe's url, filling each {name} from the task, explore only when it fails, and say in your report that it did.\n- With no tab given, start with browser_act navigate to the start url: it opens tofu's own tab, and every later step works there. When they do not, fix the filters, or report the mismatch rather than open a wrong result.\n- A video player, a menu or a card whose controls are hidden shows them on hover: hover its ref, and the result lists the controls that appeared, with their refs, to click next.\n- A dialog marked scrollable scrolls by its ref. When a click says it is covered, scroll the container or close what covers it.\n- Stay in your tab. Do not open a tab to research. When a click opens one, the next actions work there.\n- A sponsored or ad result is not the organic one.\n- When an action is refused as repeated, the page is not changing: try another ref or another way.\n- After two ways to reach a state have failed, such as a widget that ignores clicks, reach it through the site's own url: read the parameters from the current url and the page's links, build the url with the values the task needs, navigate to it, and say in the report that you did.\n- When the task is about an animation, when something opens, closes, moves or flickers, use browser_motion: capture with the scenario file the task names, inspect a take and read its table first, and compare a before and an after label. The orchestrator waits on every word, so leave out the steps that worked. A tool answer that says it is still warming is called again, not replaced by a shell run.\n\nRun the tests that cover the change with the `test` tool, given the test file or the source file that changed, never with vitest through the shell. A vitest runner stays warm for the package, so a run after the first answers in about a second. When the tool says the project does not use vitest, run the test command it names through the shell, once.\n\n## The rules that bind you\n\n**Never weaken a test to make it pass.** A changed expectation that turns a red run green is the one action that destroys the value of the entire suite. If the expectation was genuinely wrong, say so in the report as its own finding.\n\n**A skip is a result.** Count it, name it, and say what would make it run. A skipped test reported as a pass is a lie with a green tick on it.\n\n**A number beats an adjective.** Reliable, solid and fine are not results. Runs, failures, skips and the outcomes that disagreed are.\n\n**Report the defect, do not fix it.** Write what happened, what was expected, and the steps that reproduce it, in the language of the thing being tested rather than in file paths and line numbers, because a path goes stale and the behaviour does not.\n\n**Never run a destructive action against anything real.** No production, no live account, no irreversible call. If the only environment available is the real one, refuse and say so.\n\n**Say what you could not verify.** An acceptance line you could not reach is named, with what stopped you. Silence on it reads as a pass.\n\n## The verdict\n\nOne of three, and nothing else: pass, fail, or blocked, said as the first word of your report in plain text. Blocked means the environment or a dependency stopped the work, and it is not a fail. Every role (orchestrator, sub-agent, classifier) runs what you bind with `tofu models bind <role> <provider/model>` or in Models; with nothing bound it says so in one sentence and setup asks. Keys are stored per model type: `tofu login classifier typesafe` or `openrouter`, and `tofu login llm openrouter` for a chat model on your own key. Every classifier call goes through the provider you bind.\n- When a subscription runs out, the turn moves on its own to the model you chose, with a one-line notice: `continueOnSubscription`, `subscriptionOrder` and `continueOnAPIModel` in Settings, Models & roles. With nothing set, the work stops and names the fields. The lead, its sub-agents and cron all follow it.\n- Your sub-agent binding is the model every sub-agent runs that names no model of its own; a per-agent model still wins.\n- A model or settings change reaches every open window and the session holder on the next turn, with no `/reload`.\n- `leadCache` sets how long the lead's subscription prompt cache lives: `1h` by default, `5m`, or `history-5m`.\n- A ticket's thread reads as the team talking: a spawn is one handoff line naming the engineer and its mission, with the full `brief` kept apart; an engineer says what it decided or needs in at most three sentences; proof goes in evidence entries (`tofu boardy log --evidence`) that `show --thread` folds into one count; a report says where the work ended, with a verdict and each acceptance line's state; a question and its answer read as two people; every voice names its role, harness and model. On a recorded run the thread is 78% shorter with every acceptance line still carrying its evidence.\n- Jev decides whether the lead's reply answered a message you sent mid-turn.\n- A permission request carries the agent's reason and a risk level, can be allowed for an hour, and can be revoked.\n- Every message in a session carries a typed origin, so only your own words show as you.\n- While sub-agents work and the lead waits, its status is one line: waiting, the sub-agents, and how many are in bash.\n\n### Added\n\n- Custom models: a `.json` file in `.tofu/models/llms` or `.tofu/models/classifiers`, in your home or a project, adds a model; a file tofu cannot use shows its reason and blocks nothing.\n- Over `tofu serve`: tool results carry a typed summary (exit, duration, hits, lines added and removed) and bash takes a title; Boardy rows carry type, points, reason, model and tool counts; the session trace gives every call, request and sub-agent run a start offset; `models.changed` reports a binding or model change.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- A second window finds a busy session holder wherever its temp folder is, instead of taking the session over; one that cannot reach the holder says it only follows.\n- `tofu session` says what history a session holds, fresh or carried and from where.\n\n### Upgrading\n\n- Close every tofu window and its session holder before installing, since an older holder and this build do not find each other.\n- A home that ran the lead or Jev with nothing bound now asks for a binding: run `tofu models bind orchestrator <source/model>` and `tofu models bind classifier <provider/model>` with what you used before."

A sub-agent's command still moves after 30 s.\n- When you repeat something memory already keeps, the lead is told the entry and the date and answers that it is already in force, instead of promising it again; a cron prompt is never taken for your words.\n- Over `tofu serve`, `turn.steer` takes `images` like `turn.send`.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- An image in a message sent while the lead works, queued, or sent to an idle lead beside running sub-agents reaches the lead; before, under a session holder, only its `[Image #N]` text did.\n- A message typed while only sub-agents run is sent and starts the lead at once, and the status reads lead idle, free to talk, instead of queued and waiting on the sub-agents.\n- The lead's end-of-turn board check stays quiet when nothing on the board changed or your message is about something else, so the same status line is not repeated every turn.\n- A ticket a lead files for another board lands in that board's triage, and the tool says where.\n- Memory saves made at once each keep their own id and none is lost; a replace keeps its id and scope and shows once."

A sub-agent that ends without `finish` is sent back once, then ends blocked. A model that answers twice with nothing at all fails with a sentence saying it answered with nothing."

## Manual

Not offline. Each is driven by hand, with these steps, on both builds.

### 1. login claude-sub and codex-sub

OAuth against the vendor, which an offline run cannot answer

1. build both exes, then for each: set TOFU_CLAUDE_TOKEN_URL and TOFU_CODEX_TOKEN_URL to a local stub that answers the token exchange
2. tofu login llm claude-sub --paste with a mock code, in a home made fresh in the run, and the same for codex-sub
3. tofu login --status --json on both builds, diff after masking the token expiry
4. drive chat --source claude-sub and --source codex-sub on a cassette, both builds, diff

### 2. live sub turns

a real wire to the vendor

1. point TOFU_CLAUDE_BASE_URL and TOFU_CODEX_SOCKET_URL at a recording stub and run tofu run with the same task on both builds, diff the requests the stub saw
2. the orchestrator runs one real claude-sub session in the interface on the candidate build at the end

### 3. usage and quota

the vendor usage endpoints

1. stub the usage URLs, run tofu usage --json on both builds, diff
2. drive quota --quota inputs/quota.json is in the catalog and covers the footer and /status

### 4. openrouter, meta, typesafe and brave key check

each key check is a network call

1. openrouter and meta: point TOFU_OPENROUTER_API_URL and TOFU_META_BASE_URL at a stub answering 200, run tofu login llm openrouter and tofu login llm meta with a fake key on both builds, diff
2. typesafe and brave have no URL override, so only the refused path is in the catalog (login/typesafe key, login/brave key)

### 5. jev paths

every jev answer is a classifier call

1. start a local stub answering the jev wire and set TOFU_JUDGE_ENDPOINT to it with a fake key in a fresh home
2. run tofu judge, tofu check, tofu sift --arm jev, tofu run --gate enforce and drive with a gate ask on both builds, diff
3. the dry runs and the no-key answers are in the catalog (judge/dry run, judge/no key, check/no key, sift/jev no key, run/gate enforce without a classifier)

### 6. learn scan model step

the scan calls a model and has no cassette path

1. run tofu learn on a fixed project on both builds with a live key, compare the proposals by hand

### 7. browser and chrome extension host

Chrome and HKCU are the person's own

1. start a fake relay on HOME/.tofu/browser/relay.sock as cmd/tofu/browser_test.go does
2. run tofu browser tabs, read, observe, click, open, close and batch on both builds against it, diff
3. never run browser install, uninstall or profile login against the real machine

### 8. drive desk and flows 12 to 14

tofu-desktop renders pixels

1. run tofu serve --stdio --cassette with the desk core cassettes on both builds and diff the transcripts; the serve catalog already covers every method
2. render the desk on both builds and compare screenshots by eye

### 9. update install, models reload and query.update

the release and model registries are on the network

1. serve a copy of the release json on a local port, set TOFU_UPDATE_API and TOFU_UPDATE_TARGET to a scratch copy of the exe, run tofu update on both builds, diff
2. set TOFU_MODELS_REGISTRY_URL to a local copy of the registry, run tofu models reload --json on both builds, diff after sorting the provider rows

### 10. ctrl+g editor and the clipboard

ctrl+g opens EDITOR and /copy writes the person's clipboard

1. set EDITOR to a script that appends a line to its file, drive ctrl+g by hand in a terminal on both builds, compare the composer
2. paste is in the catalog through drive --clipboard (drive/flow 10-steer-image)

## Unreachable

| item | why |
|---|---|
| models/reload | the providers it fetches fail in the order they finish, so two runs of one build print them in a different order |
| flows 4, 6, 7 and 9 | bench/flows seams them inside its own runner (a panic hook, a cap, a fold cassette built at run time, a survive kill), so a script alone does not replay them; bench/flows itself runs them |
| slash /copy, /copy-call and /quote | tofu drive leaves the app's Copy unset, so the app writes the real Windows clipboard; the hook needed is a Copy sink in cmd/tofu/drive.go beside the --clipboard reader |
| serve session.history right after turn.completed | one build answers from the live event lines (turn.started first, 14 lines) or from the persisted log (session.updated first, 6 lines) depending on timing, so two runs of one build differ; session-history-empty covers the method |
| gate ask keys 1 to 3 | the ask card only shows after jev answers ask, and no offline classifier exists; needs a TOFU_JUDGE_ENDPOINT stub |
| ctrl+g editor | it opens EDITOR in a terminal that drive does not have |
| tofu with no arguments, tofu --profile and tofu --temporary-project in a terminal | the app needs a real terminal; without one the catalog covers the refusal (app/no terminal and the rest), and drive covers the app itself |
| --profile output | verbs.md section 4 says profiles are not diffed, and the profile is timing |
| browser install, uninstall, profile new, login, stop and remove | they write HKCU or start Chrome on the person's machine |
| browser tabs, read, observe, click, fill, select, press, scroll, back, open, close, batch, build, bench, motion | they talk to the person's real Chrome through the relay |
| update without --check | it replaces the installed exe |
| learn | the scan step calls a model with no cassette path |
